📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that jamie Gittens has withdrawn from the England Under-21 squad. He suffered an ankle injury during Tuesday’s qualifier against Kazakhstan at Molineux. The Chelsea winger left the ground on crutches. He has returned to Stamford Bridge, where the Jamie Gittens injury will now be assessed by the club’s medical staff.

Sources indicate that gittens picked up the knock after a challenge during the second half of England’s win over Kazakhstan. He was withdrawn as a precaution. He did not take any further part in the match. England have been careful not to overstate the problem and no further reports have come out further.

The 21-year-old struggled to put weight on the affected ankle and was seen limping around Molineux after full time. That prompted an immediate release back to his club, rather than any attempt to assess him further in camp.

England Under-21 boss Lee Carsley addressed the injury directly after the game. He confirmed the nature of the knock and the decision to send Gittens home.

“Jamie got a kick on his ankle,” Carsley stated after the match. “We never take any risks. With the age of these players, we don’t ever keep them in camp to see how they are. He will go back.”.

England’s statement on the squad changes, detailed in a report from Football.London, confirmed the wider fallout from the fixture.

“Mukasa’s call-up follows the withdrawal of Chelsea’s Jamie Gittens and Norwich City pair Kellen Fisher and Ben Chrisene through injury,” the statement read. West Ham midfielder Divine Mukasa has been called up as cover for all three.

Gittens has been an unused substitute in every Premier League fixture Chelsea have played this season, with his only two appearances under Xabi Alonso coming in the Carabao Cup. Those minutes have offered him little platform after his significant summer move.

According to recent reports, alonso’s squad selection has been a talking point since he took charge. Our earlier look at Xabi Alonso’s squad choices at Stamford Bridge covered how competitive things have become. An ankle injury will not change his pecking order in the short term. It does, though, remove any chance of him pushing his case this week.

Chelsea’s break has brought other headlines too. Cole Palmer also withdrew, for entirely different reasons, after his recall by senior boss Thomas Tuchel to the full England squad. Chelsea will be watching both returns closely before domestic football resumes.

Chelsea have not yet issued a formal update on the severity of the injury. Any recovery timeline will depend on an assessment by the club’s medical team once Gittens is back at Cobham. Nothing beyond the crutches seen at Molineux has been confirmed.

Given his limited game time this season, the immediate concern is less about missed fixtures than a setback to his integration under Alonso. Fans can follow how the squad shapes up before the next fixtures through our recent line-up updates. Further news on Gittens is expected once Chelsea’s medical staff finish their evaluation.

  • Koné remains under contract at the Stadio Olimpico, and he has become a key part of Roma’s midfield since his move from Borussia Mönchengladbach.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that roma have put an £86m (€100m) price tag on Manu Koné, according to Gazzetta dello Sport, reviving the Manu Koné Chelsea transfer link that first emerged over the summer. Roma want any interested club, including Chelsea, to know the price before serious talks can even begin.

Koné remains under contract at the Stadio Olimpico, and he has become a key part of Roma’s midfield since his move from Borussia Mönchengladbach. The Gazzetta report reads like a warning to potential buyers rather than proof of any talks between the two clubs.

Roma sporting director Tony D’Amico has confirmed Chelsea made contact late in the summer window, though he was quick to draw a clear line under how far things went.

According to recent reports, “There was an inquiry and some preliminary contact with Chelsea on the final day of the transfer window. No official offers arrived that would allow us to approach the player. Something was imagined that simply didn’t happen. There was no official offer; the final day of the transfer window got everyone a little worked up.”.

D’Amico’s comments confirm Chelsea looked at signing Koné before the deadline, but they stop well short of showing an official bid was ever made. He also explained why Roma had no wish to sell a key player so close to the window closing.

Sources indicate that “Before the match against Fiorentina (on 24 August), I noted it would be difficult for us to deprive ourselves of vital players so near to the end of the transfer session, and so it proved. Kone is an important player, we’re happy he stayed with us, and we’re confident he’ll give his contribution during the season.”.

Industry observers note that chelsea’s midfield has changed shape under Xabi Alonso since the summer, with Morgan Rogers arriving to add depth and competition for places. That signing came during a window that also saw exits acceleration under Xabi Alonso, as the head coach reshaped his squad around his own style.

Koné’s ball winning and his range of progressive passing would suit Alonso well, should Chelsea ever revisit their interest. Supporters have already seen how Alonso rotates his midfield for the biggest games, including the recent derby line-up selections against Brentford.

In a recent development, for now, Rogers and Chelsea’s existing central options give Alonso enough cover without needing an immediate signing. Roma’s reluctance to sell also means any deal would need patience rather than a quick resolution.

It has been revealed that nothing in D’Amico’s comments suggests Roma are open to a sale in the near term, and Koné has given no sign that he wants to leave. The £86m valuation, reported by Football London, stands as Roma’s marker rather than an asking price involved with Chelsea.

According to recent reports, will Chelsea return with a more formal approach in a future window? D’Amico’s comments give no hint either way. The Manu Koné Chelsea transfer link is unlikely to fade given Chelsea’s history of scouting France’s leading midfielders, but any fresh move will have to wait for Roma’s stance to soften.

Portsmouth v West Ham United EFL Championship, Fratton Park, Tuesday 24 November 2026, 7.45pm GMT.

This is a crucial match for West Ham and Scott Parker, who has probably endured the shortest honeymoon period of any Hammers manager in recent memory. His first three games have produced a rousing comeback against Cardiff City, a forgettable defeat at Blackburn Rovers and Saturday’s frustrating 1-1 draw with Preston North End.

Recent findings suggest that west Ham dominated possession and registered 30 attempts against Preston, yet never really looked clinical enough to score the winner. Indeed, had the referee awarded another 20 minutes of injury time, I’m still not convinced we would have found a second goal.

According to recent reports, parker is still waiting for his first victory as West Ham head coach, and Tuesday’s trip to Fratton Park represents another difficult assignment. Portsmouth have lost just once in eight Championship matches and sit only one point and two places behind the tenth-placed Hammers.

It has been revealed that ordinarily, one might expect Parker to do some tinkering after failing to beat the team at the bottom of the division. However, I suspect he won’t make sweeping changes because he was very pleased with the way his team performed against Preston.

Edson Alvarez – likely to become key in Parker’s prepares this season.

Parker said he got almost everything he wanted from the performance apart from the result, while describing Finlay Herrick and Edson Álvarez as “brilliant” in his post-match assessment. I’m not quite sure I would agree with that overall verdict, although the return of Álvarez was unquestionably a bonus.

Industry observers note that the Mexican looked decent on his return to the team and provided some much-needed protection in front of the back four. Parker has probably made it clear that, for the remainder of this season, West Ham will play with a recognised holding midfielder.

It has been revealed that without wishing to sound like a scratched record, I still believe Jarrod Bowen needs to be used more centrally. Parker appeared to have been given the keys to unlocking West Ham’s attacking potential against Cardiff, but unfortunately he seems to have kept them in his back pocket ever since.

Bowen remains our most dangerous attacking player, yet watching him pinned to the right flank against Preston was depressing. West Ham lacked magic, invention and somebody willing to take responsibility in the areas where matches are won.

It has been revealed that mohamadou Kanté can consider himself unlucky not to have featured at all against Preston because he has been one of West Ham’s better players this season. There is an argument for playing him in the attacking midfield position at Portsmouth, where his pace and direct running could give Parker’s team something different.

However, I don’t think Parker will throw the baby out with the bathwater. He has already spoken about remaining stable and consistent, so I expect Divine Mukasa to retain his place behind Joël Piroe.

Piroe should continue up front, as much because of the lack of convincing alternatives as anything else. Manor Solomon could return on the left, with Parker perhaps deciding that his experience is better suited to a difficult night at Fratton Park.

Recent findings suggest that I suspect there will be a change at left-back, with Ollie Scarles coming into the team. Max Kilman is available again after completing his one-match suspension and should immediately return alongside Konstantinos Mavropanos.

Sources indicate that according to the club’s official team news, Alphonse Areola and Kyle Walker-Peters continue to be assessed. Unless Walker-Peters is unexpectedly declared fit, Joël Veltman should remain at right-back.

Sources indicate that portsmouth possess a worse attack than West Ham but a better defence, so this is unlikely to be an open game. They are only two places and one point behind us, while their recent results suggest Parker’s team will have to work extremely hard for anything at Fratton Park.

West Ham’s failure to convert possession into goals remains the obvious concern. However, if Parker can keep things tight defensively and finally find a way to make one of our attacking opportunities count, I believe the Hammers can edge it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anyone hoping for bold action on climate change has many reasons to be disappointed by the latest United Nations climate summit, COP31, which concluded in a dramatic overtime session on 22 November.
  • The last COP climate talk to break down this badly was the Copenhagen summit in 2009.
  • Recent findings suggest that the COP31 outcome wasn’t inevitable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anyone hoping for bold action on climate change has many reasons to be disappointed by the latest United Nations climate summit, COP31, which concluded in a dramatic overtime session on 22 November. After gathering for nearly two weeks in the beach resort city of Antalya, Turkey, in what will probably be the hottest year on record, representatives from nearly all the world’s countries failed to agree on a strategy to tackle climate change. Almost 100 nations walked out without signing a ‘cover decision’ — a non-binding statement meant to push for ambitious action — because the document did not call on the world to transition away from fossil fuels.

The last COP climate talk to break down this badly was the Copenhagen summit in 2009. After that meeting, the late geoscientist James Lovelock commented: “I don’t think we’re yet evolved to the point where we’re clever enough to handle as complex a situation as climate change.” Seventeen years and an increase in atmospheric carbon dioxide levels of almost 40 parts per million later, and governments still seem unable to overcome national differences for the benefit of the planet.

Recent findings suggest that the COP31 outcome wasn’t inevitable. There had been some optimism among climate watchers ahead of the summit that, despite ongoing geopolitical conflicts, rising energy prices and energy shortages would spur countries to support a transition away from burning coal, oil and gas — the biggest drivers of climate change. But when language targeting fossil fuels disappeared from the draft cover decision after lobbying by oil-rich nations, a coalition of around 90 countries, led by the European Union and small island states, rejected the agreement.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Storey was an influential member of one of the most successful sides in the club’s history.
  • Storey was a key figure in the famous run as he helped keep the FA Cup hopes alive with a display against Stoke City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal have expressed their condolences in the passing of former player Peter Storey.

Storey was an influential member of one of the most successful sides in the club’s history. The midfielder appeared in 501 games for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, winning the First Division and FA Cup during the 1970/71 season.

Storey was a key figure in the famous run as he helped keep the FA Cup hopes alive with a display against Stoke City.

Sources indicate that A statement from the club confirmed his death on Tuesday (17th November). The club will pay tribute to Storey in their Champions League tie against Borussia Dortmund on 24th November.

Storey signed as an apprentice with Arsenal in 1961, and made his first-team debut in October 1965 in a game against Leicester City.

He was later converted to a central midfielder by manager Bertie Mee and coach Don Howe. Storey became an invaluable member of the squad due to his aggressive play, work-rate and versatility.

In 1970 Storey was part of the side that won the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, and the following year Arsenal won the league and FA Cup double.

It has been revealed that storey played a key role in an amazing FA Cup semi-final in April 1971. After Arsenal had looked like they were losing, Storey scored a last-minute penalty to make it 2-2.

Arsenal won the replay to get to the final, beating Liverpool to win their first-ever double.

According to recent reports, storey scored 17 goals in 501 games for Arsenal. This puts him in joint 8th place in the most appearances for the club.

Recent findings suggest that storey enjoyed success at club level and earned his first cap for England in 1971. He earned a total of 19 caps for England.

He played for England until 1973. In 1977, Storey left Arsenal to join Fulham, meaning he had a 12-year stint at the north London club.

He played 19 games for Fulham before retiring from professional football in 1978.

Following his football career, Storey had a difficult time. He was imprisoned for a number of crimes. In 2010, he wrote an autobiography, True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man, detailing these events in his life.

Industry observers note that he will be remembered in Arsenal history for his impressive contribution to the club. Having made 501 appearances for the club, he was a key member of the squad that won the Double in 1971.

Playing against Borussia Dortmund will be a great way for fans to pay tribute to one of the key players in a special time in the history of the club.

Frosinone have definitely been one of the surprises of the season so far. After a very strong Serie B campaign with 81 points and only three games lost, they secured direct promotion to the top tier (finishing second) and have been making the most of the adventure.

It’s the 56-year-old’s second attempt at Serie A after coaching Cremonese for half a season in 2022-23. He didn’t manage a single win then, so you can definitely say that the performance so far has been great revenge for him.

➤ Milan have failed to win four of their last seven Serie A games played after the international break (D2 L2). On the other hand, Frosinone are unbeaten in three of their last five top-flight matches immediately following Italy matches (W2 D1).

Recent findings suggest that since Frosinone like to play on the counterattacks, one player who I think could be crucial for Milan is Musah. Further up the pitch, I’m excited to see Moreira. He got himself a goal in Belgium’s win over Italy and he has looked a lot better on the right flank ever since the derby performance. He can definitely make the difference with his skill.

Industry observers note that as for Frosinone, it’s obvious that Calo is the man whom Milan will want to stop. He likes to dictate the play and if he’s allowed too much time on the ball, identifying his teammates in good positions, then there could be trouble for the Rossoneri.

Recent findings suggest that it will also be interesting to see if Birigilea can fill the shoes of Raimondo. He bagged a brace against Lecce but in the last two games, he failed to find the back of the net. He will surely be keen to get back on target.

A lot of people are expecting this to be a high-scoring affair and that’s a very reasonable take, given how both teams play. That mentioned, I think this could be one where Milan actually get their defence in order and don’t concede, even if that might be a somewhat optimistic prediction.

The 125th cap was no different to the first for Harry Kane, who has now been in the business of goal accumulation for so long that it is only at the landmark moments, that all of us are obliged to step back and take in the full scale of the work he has created.

It has been revealed that peter Shilton took 20 years to rack up his 125 caps, while for Kane it has been just 11 – and then there are the goals. Two more on Tuesday took him to 91 which means that only 12 other England players in history have more England caps than Kane has England goals. This unassuming man from Chingford, who looks like a mildly rebellious academic from the late 1950s, was at it again: the first-time strike, the back-post header. He has some misses across these 11 years, most infamously from the penalty spot against France at the Qatar World Cup almost four years ago, so, yes, there are some regrets too. But what sticks is the way he has taken his chances – again and again.

According to recent reports, following his debut goal in 2015 against Lithuania, Kane has missed just 27 of the 152 England games since. He has added to the total like a great Test batsman patiently moving the scoreboard along. There was a bad run without goals in 2020 and before that in 2018. He scored only five in his first 17 caps and then scored 14 in his next 10. Against a very mediocre Czech Republic team this was classic late-era Kane, picking his moments and taking those chances with the usual absence of nerves. He was even substituted before the end.

The more you think about the hundred… you don’t always get there.” There has still not been the elusive major trophy in the Kane England years but there has been success relative to the three decades that came before it. Semi-finals, finals – a good team if not a winning team.

According to recent reports, at the centre of it has been a man around whom there has never been any scandal or, by the usual measure, much that might be described as spectacular. Rather it has been the scope of Kane’s career that is the most striking. The volume of the goals, of appearances, the capacity to be available – to play, to score – and the absolute quality of the player himself. He is determined to wring the very last drop out of his talent and usually refuses to acknowledge the prospect of the end, although there was a nod to it this time. “At some stage you know this opportunity isn’t going to be here,” he stated. “I’m not going to be around forever, and I still hope that’s a long way away. But ultimately, of course, there’s times you’re tired or you’re injured, but I know I’ll miss it when it’s done. I try to always remind myself that and always try to make myself available.”.

He talks like a different person to the one he was even five years ago – with a confidence and certainty about his place in the world. As opposed to the younger Kane, who seemed to regard everything outside his goalscoring tunnel vision with a general sense of bemusement.

It has been revealed that “Availability,” he said, “is one of the biggest strengths you can have at this level for any coach.” He was keen to emphasise his “all-round leadership” too, “a lot of assets off the pitch”. He still measures himself in goals, of course, and perhaps there will be a Ballon d’Or too later this month – a prize that has eluded generations of England players before him who have won much more for their clubs than Kane has done. The good news for Kane is that his last England years will be spent in a very good England team – one which was on another level to its opposition on this occasion too.

No team in the top tier of the Nations League has scored more goals than England – 14 in the last four match days. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tonight’s mid table clash, yep, 10th play 12th, brought back memories of a West Ham United game in Division 1 back in 1992/1993. Without wanting to sound like Paul Whitehouse’s legendary Fast Show character, Ron Manager, and his famous cry of “jumpers for goalposts”, my mind drifted back to the footballing world of the 1990s this morning.

It has been revealed that I recall watching the game on ITV, on a programme called the London Match, hosted by Ian St John, and a quick search on YouTube found some footage, with Greavsies side kick being  joined by Glenn Hoddle. Jim Rosenthal was at Fratton Park as part of the commentary team.

Portsmouth featured in the FA Cup semi finals the previous season. West Ham drew 1-1 with Derby County the week before the game, Trevor Morley cancelling out a clearance by Mitchell Thomas which had cannoned off Ludo for an own goal earlier in the game, which kept the Hammers in the top six.

Bonzo was the West Ham manager in 1992.

With Billy Bonds at the helm, West Ham were unbeaten in six games, yet faced a Pompey team that had only played twice at home, won both and not conceded. They boasted the prolific striker Guy Whittingham up front, and with Jim Smith in the manager’s seat, were stiff opposition for us. Yet as he remarked in the warm up the Hammers were one of the favourites to go up.

Pre game the major news was welcoming back Julian Dicks our skipper who came off a three match ban.

The Hammers took the lead just before half time with Clive Allen (main  pic) scoring, yet despite an onslaught of the Pompey goal in the second half they couldn’t add to their tally.

Trevor Morley was denied by the woodwork, while Martin Allen (who was never afraid to shoot from distance) also had a long effort saved.

Happy memories, as it was a time when the club had a greater connection to us, the fans.

I’d settle for a clean sheet and a win tonight, how football has changed or as Ron said “Isn’t it, wasn’t it, marvellous”.

The Danny Drinkwater Chelsea story still carries a sting. Five years at Stamford Bridge gave him plenty of time to think about how it all turned out, and his own verdict is not a happy one.

Drinkwater opened up in a Truth or Padel appearance alongside David Ornstein. He said the move was one he could never have turned down, even with the benefit of hindsight. “No, I don’t regret moving. I regret, in hindsight, how it’s turned out. I think I could never turn it down,” he said.

It has been revealed that strip away the headlines and the numbers alone tell an uncomfortable story. Drinkwater spent five years on Chelsea’s books. In that time he made just 23 appearances, according to the original interview report.

Do the maths and it barely comes to five games a year. That is a thin return for a central midfielder signed to compete for a first-team place. It is also the kind of record that rarely sits well at a club of Chelsea’s size and ambition.

Chelsea’s best attacking spells over a similar stretch of seasons look far more productive, as our striker rankings show. Set next to those numbers, Drinkwater’s five quiet years stand out even more starkly.

Five years. Twenty three games. These numbers alone explains why this transfer still gets talked about by Drinkwater, long after the headlines faded.

Industry observers note that the numbers only tell part of the story. A string of incidents turned a quiet, underwhelming spell into something far more pointed.

In a recent development, drinkwater had a training-ground bust-up while out on loan. He was also involved in an on-pitch brawl with Chelsea’s own under-23s side. Flashpoints between a first-team player and a development squad are rare at any club, let alone one with Chelsea’s standards.

According to recent reports, taken alone, either incident might have passed as a bad day. Taken together, it became harder to see Drinkwater simply as an unlucky squad player who could not catch a break.

In a recent development, the most serious moment came during his time at Aston Villa. Drinkwater headbutted team-mate Jota and was fined two weeks’ wages for it. He states the consequences at Chelsea did not stop there.

“They didn’t formally ban me, but I got removed from the first team building after the incident at Villa,” Drinkwater said.

Sources indicate that one off-field incident, at another club, pushed him out of the manager’s day-to-day looks back home. No formal punishment at Chelsea followed. The effect was much the same.

Sources indicate that chelsea fans saw a similar breakdown of trust play out when Graham Potter struggled to win over the dressing room during another difficult Chelsea transition. Trust can break down fast once results or behaviour turn against the person at the centre of it.

Sources indicate that drinkwater’s comments matter beyond his own career. They are a reminder that saying yes to a significant move does not guarantee it will work once a player walks through the door.

That tension has not gone away. Chelsea’s current transfer business, covered in our transfer watch, reveals the club still weighing major calls on players whose futures depend on more than form alone.

It has been revealed that squad management under Xabi Alonso, assessed in our bomb squad verdict, raises a familiar problem. Players who fall outside a manager’s looks rarely find a quick way back in, whether the exile is formal or not.

Drinkwater never found his way back into Chelsea’s aims after the Villa incident. His account of the Danny Drinkwater Chelsea years stands as a blunt warning. A move that looks impossible to refuse can still become one of the hardest spells of a career.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club opting to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.
  • The departure is understood to be amicable and won’t take immediate effect.
  • The story was first reported by Matt Law of The Telegraph and Nizaar Kinsella of BBC Sport, with Ben Jacobs subsequently providing further details about how Chelsea intend to operate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club opting to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

The departure is understood to be amicable and won’t take immediate effect. Stewart could continue attending matches before formally leaving, following discussions with co-owner Behdad Eghbali over the club’s evolving sporting structure.

The story was first reported by Matt Law of The Telegraph and Nizaar Kinsella of BBC Sport, with Ben Jacobs subsequently providing further details about how Chelsea intend to operate.

Stewart arrived from Monaco in October 2022 as technical director before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley in February 2023.

Chelsea’s day-to-day sporting leadership will now be shared between Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields, each with defined responsibilities.

In a recent development, winstanley will continue overseeing transfer negotiations, player contracts and several departments at Cobham, including medical and performance operations. Shields’ work centres on the academy and player pathways, while Jewell has wider responsibilities across the BlueCo operation, including Strasbourg.

According to Jacobs, discussions about restructuring began in April and accelerated following the appointment of Xabi Alonso as head coach.

Stewart had overseen investment in Chelsea’s data analysis operation, although Jewell and Shields have increasingly taken responsibility for using that information in recruitment and talent identification.

Dave Fallows will remain involved in an advisory capacity, rather than taking on a fixed day-to-day portfolio.

In a recent development, the changes are being described as a natural evolution of Chelsea’s sporting model. There is no suggestion that Stewart’s departure followed a breakdown in relations, and the club are not at the moment planning to recruit a replacement.

There will be no live UK television coverage of Chelsea’s return to Premier League action against Bournemouth on Saturday afternoon.

That means supporters unable to attend will need to follow the match through other channels, rather than watching it live on Sky Sports or TNT Sports.

Although the game will not be televised live in the UK, supporters can follow developments through the official Chelsea website and the Premier League website.

The Saturday 3pm blackout prevents live domestic television broadcasts during the restricted period, although overseas coverage may be available through broadcasters holding the relevant rights.

Highlights will be available after the match through the usual broadcast and digital channels, subject to their respective release schedules.

Chelsea will then turn their attention to a trip to Everton on Saturday, 17 October, with that fixture scheduled for a 12.30pm kick-off at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

For Alonso, the Bournemouth match provides the immediate opportunity to resume Chelsea’s domestic campaign following the international break.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just for a change one of West Ham’s young signings is being lauded rather than slated today – Edvin Austbø came in for a fair degree of stick in a report yesterday claiming he was heading towards ‘flop’ status – but the club’s pursuit and purchase of Dan Cummings from Celtic last summer is being complimented by his new manager.

Cummings went out on loan this month to fifth tier Aldershot Town and came off the bench to score within six minutes of his debut, as we covered yesterday.

As reported this afternoon by insidefutbol.com, The Shots’ manager Scott Davies has been waxing lyrical over Cummings and West Ham’s shrewd purchase of their future star:.

“Aldershot Town boss Scott Davies has admitted that he can see why West Ham United invested heavily in Daniel Cummings, following the former Celtic talent’s promising start to life at the National League side:.

“To bring on someone like Dan’s quality on with sort of half an hour to go, or 25 minutes to go, and then he gets a goal within five minutes is like a dream world for me as a manager.

“And for us as a management team, that takes the pressure off.

Listen, he’s been great in training and you can see the quality he’s got. No wonder why West Ham bought him for a lot of money. So, we’re really lucky to have him on loan and hopefully we’ll see more of him in weeks to come.”.

£600,000 in Aldershot’s world is a lot of money indeed for a teenager: For West Ham a mere drop in the ocean but good to hear that Cummings is making all the right moves.

Hopefully, the start of a stream of good news coming out of Hampshire as the young Scot finds his feet.

Raya has been ruled out of tonight’s Champions League game following a shoulder problem which he picked up in Saturday’s 2-2 draw with Newcastle United.

Recent findings suggest that whilst the initial diagnosis is good news, surgery is not required. Further tests will determine Raya’s recovery period.

Sources indicate that as previously mentioned, Kepa will be stepping in for Raya at St James’ Park. Moreover, Arteta has stated his preferred choice of player in this situation. It seems that Illan Meslier will miss out on the opportunity to play this time.

According to recent reports, as well as playing for Arsenal, the Spaniard has formerly played in the Champions League for Chelsea and Real Madrid. He has already appeared 14 times for the Gunners. Including in the league stage match which saw them beat Kairat Almaty.

Recent findings suggest that whilst Kepa has typically been second choice to Raya, his game time has mostly been in the EFL Cup. He will now need to prove himself as a trustworthy option for Arsenal should Raya be injured or otherwise unable to play.

Industry observers note that as well as being a good goalkeeper, Raya is also good at passing and positioning. This in turn assists Arsenal in attacking from the back line.

Ex-Arsenal midfielder Paul Merson has acknowledged the quality that Spanish goalkeepers have at creating good defensive and central positioning. This can frequently be an under-recognised yet important component in Arsenal’s build-up play.

Like Arsenal, Kepa will also have to remain calm when playing out from the back. Although Kepa does not necessarily need to replicate all of Raya’s qualities, he will need to have good decision-making skills as well as good communication.

Sources indicate that meslier is still in contention, having played in the Carabao Cup game against Fleetwood Town. Kepa has been Arsenal’s number two keeper in the Premier League and was able to rush on in for Raya when he was substituted at Newcastle.

It does seem that Kepa is the obvious option, and he can further cement his position in Arteta’s team.

Arsenal’s schedule is demanding. They are playing Manchester City on a Sunday and there are also worries about Raya’s fitness. So far, the club has not yet received medical information on Raya’s status.

Then there is Dortmund. They have already secured victories in their first four games in the Champions League and are level on points with Arsenal in the league section.

Kepa does not have a great deal of flexibility. Arsenal require the fresh goalkeeper to offer them security.

In case Raya needs more time to recover, it is necessary for Arteta to be able to guarantee that there is an effective replacement.

For Kepa, it is equally an opportunity to prove that he can assume this leadership position for the team during key moments.

According to recent reports, the first matter the Portuguese forward needs to address is his finishing. In four matches – against Juventus, Lecce, Bologna, and Inter – he failed to register a single shot, while in two others (against Lazio and Genoa), he didn’t manage to hit the target.

That is simply not enough for a striker who cost €70m, plus bonuses and commissions. However, according to the former Manchester United manager, the fault does not lie with Gonçalo and instead is a team concern.

We need to support him better through more possession and quick passing combinations in the final third.

In a recent development, “My goal is to win matches while helping the players perform at their best. We signed Ramos to score goals, but right now, he is helping me more than I am helping him.” A candid admission in defence of the striker he personally pushed to sign.

Compared to the win in Genoa two Sundays ago, Amorim is leaning toward not fielding four attacking players (Moreira, Cisse, Pulisic, and Ramos) from the start.

In a recent development, “The choice of formation depends on the opponent and the team’s current state. I don’t believe that scoring more goals or winning more matches is necessarily linked to fielding more attacking players. Frosinone is an attractive side to watch, and speed is their primary weapon,” Amorim added.

Recent findings suggest that “We rank second in Serie A for the number of sprints, and we have the tools to counter both their pace and their one-on-one ability on the flanks. We’ll need to be focused, as they commit more players to the final third than we do and are more clinical than us when winning the ball back.

It has been revealed that “As for our season so far? I’m not satisfied with fourth place or all of our performances. We need to play better and achieve more in Europe, but we have grown as a team and in our overall attitude. We must keep moving in this direction.”.

Recent findings suggest that he concluded by sharing a Christmas wish regarding the transfer market: “January signings shouldn’t be based on the current league table, but rather on long-term planning. Recent findings suggest that arsenal were caught offside four times in the opening 16 minutes vs Leeds. That's 24 offsides in Premier League games for the season so far, which is at least twice as many as any every other team (Leeds, Brighton, Spurs 12 each) . https://t.co/jnTQah5bh4.

Great save from Raya when Gudmundsson’s thumping volley on the end of Bogle’s superb, deep cross is blocked at the near post. Okafor set the move going with a fine crossfield pass.

Arsenal keep the ball but are being pushed back and forced to horseshoe from right to left wing. Madueke suddenly accelerates and drives towards the box to belt over a cross that havertz, from a very tight angle, heads miles over.

It has been revealed that it feels like there’s 15 yellow shirts out there, which is testament to the organisation (and physical size?) of this Leeds team. They have been the better side. Tanaka and Stach are frustrating the Arsenal midfielders.

Two more Leeds names in the book: Ampadu for a late foul on Odegaard and Farke’s when the fourth official dobs him in to referee for something he said.

The crowd is growing frustrated by how well Leeds are playing and how little space they are allowing Arsenal.

Recent findings suggest that okafor overhits a pass in from the left that would have put Stach through on to the keeper. Then Tanaka is penalised for bodychecking Lewis-Skelly and goes into the book.

Oakfor rolls the ball into an empty net when Raya runs out but the whistle had already gone because Calafiori had triggered the trap perfectly.

Recent findings suggest that chances at both ends as Raya comes off his line, swats a punch to Amapdu who tries to loop it over him. Raya runs back to catch it and drifts very close to his goal-line. Tanaka loses the ball in midfield and Arsenal pile forward but Leeds mass the ranks of their defence and block the path to goal until Justin is fouled to relieve the siege.

In a recent development, calafiori drives past Bogle and whips over a cross that is behind Havertz who has to backpedal to head it which robs his effort of power. Trafford drops to his knees to gather.

As TNT Sports points out, Leeds are trying to press Arsenal high but the positioning of Rice and Lewis-Skelly is much better than it was at Brighton.

Leeds’ offside trap has been functioning well and now Arsenal’s well-oiled one kicks in to catch Gudmundsson and Okafor.

Arsenal have been eager to play quick passes over the Leeds defence in these opening exchanges. Arteta’s side usually prefer to build up more slowly but they are looking for Havertz quite early. A consequence, perhaps, of Leeds pushing quite high up the pitch.

Okafor’s blistering 20-yard shot is deflected behind for a corner. The linesman’s flag was up because he noted Calvert-Lewin had moved towards the ball in an offside position but the referee overrules him.

Arsenal defend the cross solidly but Bogle is covering diligently when they try to play Madueke clear with a long ball.

Recent findings suggest that justin heads the ball to Ampadu who plays a one-two with Stach then chips the ball 40 yards, a real up and under, for Calvert-Lewin to chase. Raya beats him to it.

Industry observers note that both sides used the opportunity of the playing of The Angel to muster in huddles. Arsenal switch to their right and try to free Saka but Trafford comes out to kick it into touch.

Arsenal in red and white, Leeds in yellow and black. Ben White was looking round to see if there was anyone in the Leeds line he recognised from his excellent year’s loan with them but Marcelo Bielsa’s promotion heroes have all moved on now. In fact, with Illan Meslier, there are two at the Gunners and none at Elland Road.

Long international break, we recovered most of our players and have a point to prove after our last game.

[Declan Rice] needed that [break] after everything he’s done over the years. He has looked fresh this week.

Everyone is fit and ready to play but we have a very difficult opponent.

We know that today is one of the toughest tasks in European football. They have been the most consistent side in Europe for years. Especially after a warning shot in the last game, they will be on it today.

But we didn’t win our good start in the lottery we earned it. We travel here in confidence.

In a recent development, brighton didn’t park the bus. They went for it and pressed Arsenal. You need to do this. You have to go for it. If you sit deep their individual quality is too good. The one thing is to have a strategy and a theory but another to execute it.

Recent findings suggest that last season we faced one of the best sides in the world so we didn’t dwell on [those defeats]. If we are at our best we have a chance to compete for points.

There’s no doubt who the biggest threat to Arsenal’s defence will be today: Dominic Calvert-Lewin has four goals in six games in all competitions this season and is the top scoring Englishman in the league since the start of last season. He’s a player Arsenal once looked at signing, many years ago.

Joe Cole is trying to make a case that Manchester City are not guilty of cheating because financial doping is not the same as taking drugs or match-fixing. A man who won all his medals at Abramovich’s Chelsea indicates it ‘is not right to class it as cheating’.

This is where punditry is broken. A former player may have an opinion on the subject of finance but it does not sound as though he is particularly informed and yet he’s given time to witter on because he doesn’t ‘feel’ it’s right.

It has been revealed that right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

It was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

Arsenall need no fanfare. Until the set-back in dear old Sussex by the sea, they had looked formidable most of the time and will have been champing at the bit to get back out there and prove it was an aberration. Mikel Arteta mentioned he has doubts about Declan Rice, Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa but Ben White, Max Dowman and Chrsthian Mosquera are all available. For Leeds Joe Rodon is still out and Dan James was injured on international duty but Harry Wilson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya returned to training after knocks this week and Daniel Farke was relatively optimistic about their prospects.

Arsenal waste chances as Borussia Dortmund fight back to claim Emirates point

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal failed to improve their Champions League prospects after a disappointing 1-1 game against Borussia Dortmund in which they lost their initial lead.
  • According to recent reports, despite Viktor Gyökeres’ spectacular goal, Mikel Arteta’s men allowed Maximilian Beier to level just after the halftime break.
  • Despite winning their first three league phase games, it was an expensive night for Arsenal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal failed to improve their Champions League prospects after a disappointing 1-1 game against Borussia Dortmund in which they lost their initial lead.

According to recent reports, despite Viktor Gyökeres’ spectacular goal, Mikel Arteta’s men allowed Maximilian Beier to level just after the halftime break. Although Arsenal were presented with several good scoring opportunities, they continually lacked composure in front of goal.

Despite winning their first three league phase games, it was an expensive night for Arsenal. They have maintained their perfect record in Europe, but for just the second time in the league phase at the Emirates, the Gunners have lost points.

Arteta will also be interested to see how much effort his team expended in their pursuit of a winning goal against Manchester City on Sunday.

Arsenal began confidently and rapidly forced Dortmund to defend. Noni Madueke was troublesome on the right-hand side, and although Christos Tzolis was presented with a great chance, he failed to score from a cross.

Just ten minutes in, Madueke played a ball into the path of Gyökeres some 25 yards out. The Swedish forward then fired a curling shot over Gregor Kobel into the net.

A stunning goal from Arsenal’s forward was just what they required. Unfortunately, they were then unable to follow up this positive play.

Recent findings suggest that despite Tzolis’ effort prompting a save from Kobel, Madueke failed to score from the ball’s subsequent deflection. Likewise, Declan Rice was presented with a good opportunity when Martin Ødegaard set him up in a neat fashion.

Sources indicate that despite dominating play in the first half, Arsenal made a number of poor concluding decisions. Piero Hincapié failed to score from a good position, and Gyökeres also shot high from another good play.

Recent findings suggest that dortmund did not produce much throughout the game. However, Kepa Arrizabalaga did well to save from Joane Gadou in added time.

Arsenal should have gone into half-time with a more comfortable advantage. Instead, they gave the visitors a route back into the contest.

Shortly after play resumed, Beier failed to score despite being presented with a great chance following a low cross into the six-yard area.

Recent findings suggest that despite Arsenal successfully weathering that period of pressure, Dortmund soon retaliated. Gadou broke through the middle and passed to Beier, who then rounded Gabriel before coolly beating Kepa in the 55th minute.

Arsenal then faced a tougher challenge as they sought to add a second goal against increasingly confident Dortmund.

Arteta brought on Eberechi Eze, and the player quickly became involved. However, his shot was deflected just over the bar.

Recent findings suggest that continuing to trouble Dortmund, Madueke saw a header from Ødegaard also fly wide. A shot from Guirassy, also deflected, hit the post, and Rice then shot wide on the other side after Eze had provided an assist for him.

In a recent development, despite having 29 shots at goal, the Gunners failed to make inroads. William Saliba, too, warmed up on the touchline and then did not play. Arteta continued with his existing defensive line.

Whilst Arsenal had much to be commended for in their attacking play, especially in the first half, good chances are of little use if they are not then converted.

It has been revealed that although Arteta will recognise that he should have secured three points, Dortmund have taken a well-earned point away from north London. Now, Arsenal need to swiftly refocus on Sunday’s game against Manchester City.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that from the sound of it, West Ham United are going all-in to refresh their options in front of goal in January. The club face a crisis with none of their trio of goal scorers looking fit for purpose: The best of the three, Joel Piroe, has amassed four goals this season whilst the other two have managed just one goal apiece.

Neither Pablo Felipe nor Taty Castellanos have fulfilled the expectations that were present when they were signed in the January window at the start of this year – Taty especially was expected to boss the Championship after the Hammers were relegated but at times he’s appeared no more than a scowling misfit, unable to influence games when he’s been called upon.

‘What a waste of money” as the song goes….

Footballinsider.com – who are usually on the ball with their reporting – have it apparently on good authority that West Ham are prepared to sanction his departure in January even though the club will have to absorb yet another huge financial hit:.

“Sources: West Ham to accept Taty Castellanos loss ahead of January”.

Runs their article, detailing West Ham’s willingness to sell the forward, despite being fully aware that they’ll not see anything like the £26 million they paid for the Argentine striker just twelve months ago:.

“The 28-year-old has scored just one goal from 15 games in the Championship this season, and is performing way below the level West Ham expected from him.

Sources say that the East London outfit are prepared to sell Castellanos at a loss this winter, knowing that it will be “very difficult” to recoup the £26million they paid for him.”.

Industry observers note that this is the key: Taty had previously been linked with loan moves back to Argentina which were never really feasible. The fact that West Ham are apparently putting it ‘out there’ that they’ll take the hit in order to move the striker on means that bids should be forthcoming in the winter market from a number of clubs; several who’ll no doubt chance their arm hoping to get him for a bit of a steal.

One goal in 15 games in the second division is nothing to write home about though, and so West Ham’s approach is borne largely out of facing the undeniable fact that Castellanos has been a massive disappointment, not to mention a colossal waste of money.

A disappointing end to a disappointing match for Newcastle United Women

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1420 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Coming into the Newcastle United Women game with Nottingham Forest, both sides knew they were already eliminated from the Subway Players cup, so it was perhaps always going to be something of a ‘Dead Rubber’.
  • But with an international break looming it was still a chance for some players to stake a claim for a starting berth when the action resumes.
  • Forest made a raft of changes with Grace McEwen and Ebba Hed joining the ever-present Hannah Coan in central defence, with the trio forming a near impenetrable barrier.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Coming into the Newcastle United Women game with Nottingham Forest, both sides knew they were already eliminated from the Subway Players cup, so it was perhaps always going to be something of a ‘Dead Rubber’.

But with an international break looming it was still a chance for some players to stake a claim for a starting berth when the action resumes.

Forest made a raft of changes with Grace McEwen and Ebba Hed joining the ever-present Hannah Coan in central defence, with the trio forming a near impenetrable barrier. Both Codie Thomas and the rapid Deanne Rose operated on the flanks to great effect and caused United problems throughout.

Recent findings suggest that they went with a midfield three of Rachel Rowe sitting in front of the impressive and hard working pair Georgia Brougham and Tove Almsqvist. While Norwegian Tuva Espas and the on loan Lois Shooter partnered one another up front and looked lively.

Newcastle United Women made some subtle changes with Kayla Rendell coming back in goal, while Jemma Purfield returned to the back four. Mollie Lambert was given a chance to play in her favoured central midfield berth while Beth Lumsden shifted over to the left wing to accommodate Leanne Kiernan, who was starting against her former side.

Photo by Adam Mackman via The Mag.

Newcastle enjoyed the majority of the possession but clear cut chances were few and far between, with any opportunities that were created seemed to be snatched at or fired over the bar.

Industry observers note that the Lady Mags created a couple of opportunities early on, with Beth Lumsden and Lois Joel going close. Before Jordan Nobbs was denied by the impressive Hannah Coan inside the area with a crucial block. Nobbs had another chance soon after, but her effort from a tight angle out wide was claimed by Forest goalie Georgie Ferguson.

Forest were creating chances of their own though. Codie Thomas put the ball into the box from the left, but Tuva Espas was unable to steer her header on target. However, they were soon ahead and with it the game changed over a four minute passage of play.

Recent findings suggest that A speculative cross from Canadian international Deanne Rose out on the left was aimed at picking out Tove Almqvist but it flashed across goal and looked to be ushered out by Kayla Rendell. The goalie, on-loan from Manchester United, let the ball go past her as she assumed it was going wide of her far post, only to look foolish when the ball actually crept in off the woodwork.

Despite that setback Newcastle United Women responded well and from the ensuing kick-off were almost back level. Beth Lumsden playing on her less favoured left flank sent in a deep cross which was headed wide by Lambert.

But moments later Forest doubled their lead, when Tuva Espas forced a turnover in the United half and, spotting Rendell off her line, lobbed a perfect shot over the stranded goalie and into the net from 40 yards out.

Forest could have been three goals to the good before the break as Rachel Rowe worked the ball into the box, but was unable to find the final pass.

Newcastle had a lot of work to do in the second half but it was Forest who were looking the more dangerous side. Tove Almqvist played a ball over the Lasses defence as she tried to pick out Espas in the box, but Rendell was just able to gather it first.

It perhaps should have been 3-0 to the East Midlands side when a brilliant move was started by captain Georgia Brougham. She played the ball into Rowe who in turn found Espas, with the Norwegian international able to advance down the right before sending a great ball in for her strike partner Lois Shooter. However, United captain Rachel McLauchlan got there first and sent her clearance onto the post and very nearly into her own net before it bounced clear to safety.

It has been revealed that forest continued to create chances after that. Rowe curled an effort from the edge of the area and Rose continued to be a nuisance on the wing as she carried the ball with confidence into the final third and won a free-kick. Then did excellently to keep hold of the ball before playing it into the centre circle, to substitute Aimee Claypole, but she sent her effort straight at Rendell.

Claypole, who was on loan at Durham a couple of seasons ago, missed another chance after Freya Thomas played the ball into her feet. Her effort took a deflection before being collected once again by Rendell. Rose had another chance in stoppage time but could only find the side netting.

Industry observers note that there were very few clear cut chances in the remainder of the game with Jordan Nobbs perhaps going closest when forcing Ferguson into a low save. Codie Thomas was also strong defensively and prevented another Newcastle shot. While Purfield fired over the bar from close range before sending a corner into Ferguson’s hands.

Recent findings suggest that on what was a frustrating day for Newcastle, one bright spark was the introduction of Jessie Gale who ran her socks off after coming on, putting the Forest backline under rare pressure. The youngster’s cross/shot forced Ferguson into a save to preserve her clean sheet.

With just seconds left of stoppage time frustration began to tell and when Lois Joel shot into the net after the referee blew his whistle she was shown a yellow card, which then turned to red for dissent.

A disappointing end to what was a disappointing day.

Newcastle United: Kayla Rendell, Rachel McLauchlan (c), Hanna Németh (Aoife Mannion 88), Jemma Purfield, Kaitlyn Torpey, Lois Joel, Mollie Lambert (Jessie Gale 54), Jordan Nobbs, Beth Lumsden (Emilia Larsson 67), Martha Thomas, Leanne Kiernan (Kathleen McGovern 54).

Subs not used: Anna Tamminen, Hildur Antonsdóttir, Oona Sevenius, Gemma Evans, Abbie Richardson.

Nottingham Forest: Georgie Ferguson, Codie Thomas, Grace McEwen, Hannah Coan, Ebba Hed (Abbie Lafayette 89), Deanne Rose, Georgia Brougham (Freya Thomas 72), Tove Almqvist (Cerys Brown 89), Rachel Rowe, Tuva Espas (Aimee Claypole 62), Lois Shooter (Shania Hayles 61).

Subs not used: Katie Cox, Lucy Carney, Melissa Johnson, Lily Stevenson.

Where that leaves Newcastle United Women.

Recent findings suggest that the League Cup has adopted a Swiss League format for fixtures, with only the top eight teams of 23 progressing to the quarter finals. Both Newcastle and Forest were already mathematically eliminated before this game so the result matters very little.

It has been revealed that if you ignore the games played against WSL 1 sides Aston Villa and Everton, then Newcastle have conceded five goals in all competitions this season with four of those coming against Forest, who like United are still unbeaten in the league. That suggests the Lace City side should be one to look out for in the second half of the season, as along with Sunderland, they are the best side to face the Lady Mags so far.

Recent findings suggest that A final concern was the standard of officiating for this game. With this being a clash between two second tier sides and a premier competition, surely the standard of the referee and assistants should be better than using ones from the local Non-League circuit. There are plenty of top female officials in the top tiers of the women’s game so surely both Newcastle and Forest deserved better? A referee who needlessly sent off a player in the 94th minute and his flag waving buddies who struggled to keep up with the play throughout the game, simply isn’t good enough.

Newcastle only have one WSL 2 game remaining before the Christmas break, against Watford on Sunday, 20th December.

Sources indicate that there is now an international break before an FA Cup Third Round tie away to Manchester Unity on the 13th December with the host team based in Chadderton, Oldham. The Lasses faced the same opponents in the cup back in November 2023, winning 9-2 away from home on that occasion. Tech Report: Stunning from Matthias Jaissle, this is excellent

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Matthias Jaissle didn’t have the smoothest of arrivals at Newcastle United.
  • Disgruntled at him choosing to move on and United meeting his £9.5m release clause, Al Ahli delaying paperwork so he couldn’t start work with NUFC until only 18 days before the Premier League season kicked off.
  • A Newcastle United team that had finished 12th last season in the Premier League under an impossible 58 game schedule across all competitions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Matthias Jaissle didn’t have the smoothest of arrivals at Newcastle United.

Disgruntled at him choosing to move on and United meeting his £9.5m release clause, Al Ahli delaying paperwork so he couldn’t start work with NUFC until only 18 days before the Premier League season kicked off.

A Newcastle United team that had finished 12th last season in the Premier League under an impossible 58 game schedule across all competitions.

Coming in and inheriting a team that lost star players Tonali, Trippier, Gordon and Bruno this summer, then see a Sporting Director in control of a very defined focus on overwhelmingly recruiting younger players from overseas with the hope they will increase in quality and value across the coming years.

Fair to say this was always going to be a season of challenge for Matthias Jaissle.

Returning after the latest international break, the toughest possible matches awaited.

Reigning champions/current leaders Arsenal at St James’ Park, then away at Brighton, the only team to take any points off Arsenal in the opening ten rounds of Premier League matches.

Arsenal turned up on Saturday and did what they have done all season, they suffocated Newcastle United across the entire first half.

The Gunners passed and passed, The Magpies chased and chased.

Arsenal kept the ball, Newcastle couldn’t get it.

Matthias Jaissle’s team couldn’t get out of their own half and once the visitors took the lead, I would be surprised if any Newcastle United fan thought this would be anything other than a defeat.

In 14 Premier League and Champions League matches so far, Arsenal had won 12, lost that game at Brighton, plus drew 2-2 at Bayern Munich.

Apart from those Bayern and Brighton matches, Arsenal had conceded a grand total of three goals across the other 12 matches in the Champions League and Premier League, an average of a goal every 6+ hours in these dozen games.

Ahead of Saturday’s second half, Arsenal had Newcastle United right where they wanted them. Having dominated the opposition and taking the lead, if the home side came out and tried to get back into the game, gaps would open for the visitors to ruthlessly exploit. It is the Arsenal way.

According to recent reports, the second half about to start and Matthias Jaissle surprises everybody, three subs at such an early stage. Jacob Ramsey, Anthony Elanga and Tino Livramento replacing Sean Steur, Jacob Murphy and Amar Dedic.

From the first whistle of that second period it was Newcastle United on the front foot. Going toe to toe with Arsenal, or rather, stamping on their toes.

Sources indicate that it was exhilarating, it was what we love to see, what we had seen so many times under Eddie Howe when up against Mikel Arteta. Only Matthias Jaissle having to do it with an admittedly lower quality team, no disrespect and all that.

However, those in black and white elevated themselves as a team, they were greater than the sum of their parts.

Whatever Matthias Jaissle had said to them at the break, when added to the changes made, it was stunning.

In a recent development, arsenal were clearly not expecting this in any way, United players flooding forward in such a brave high press. Joe Willock forced Martin Odegaard into losing possession, William Osula swept forward with the loose ball and a perfect pass for Harvey Barnes to do what Harvey Barnes does.

An equaliser four minutes into the second half, so sit back and defend a 1-1?

Matthias Jaissle ordering his team to get at Arsenal, drive them back, force errors, potentially more chances….

Just after the hour mark it is Tino Livramento of all people who forces a defender, then David Raya in his six yard box into mistakes that resulted in a corner.

According to recent reports, A brilliant corner kick routine sees Arsenal out-Arsenaled, defenders blocked off and Dan Burn totally unmarked, his header parried but Joe Willock doing brilliantly to nudge the ball away from defenders despite pinned by opponents on the ground, on the line, Malick Thiaw smashing the ball home from a few inches out. Wow.

Sit back and try to defend a 2-1 for the next 37 minutes?

Matthias Jaissle insisting that his rejuvenated team keep taking the game to Arsenal.

It was 100% the correct approach.

Those remaining 37 minutes saw Newcastle United created more and better chances.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal scored a goal on the break which was brilliantly worked but still needed to go through a defender’s legs and a shot that Hornicek should probably have saved. That’s football.

Newcastle United didn’t take any of their chances and so it ended 2-2.

What a match and what an astonishing second half.

This was so so good from Matthias Jaissle.

Recent findings suggest that the coward’s way would have been to approach the second half with a mentality of keeping it tight and running the clock down. Arsenal would have kept the ball for 90% of the time, happy to take a 1-0 or 2-0 win back to London, Newcastle would have been the victims of a predictable loss.

The minority of boo boys were vocal once again at half-time with United trailing to the champions/champions-elect.

By going for it after the break, Matthias Jaissle would have known Arsenal the massive favourites to get a second goal as gaps appeared and it could easily end a very messy three or four goal home defeat.

Yet he didn’t take the coward’s way, Matthias Jaissle went for it and Newcastle United (and their fans) got the reward.

This is the kind of manager I want.

He is for sure still learning the Premier League ropes but I think he has something about him.

Certainly enough to suggest that he deserves a proper fair chance.

It has been revealed that the uber Matthias Jaissle critics say Newcastle United desperately need a Premier League proven manager. Rarely, if ever, do they ever name this mythical creature.

Sources indicate that what exactly do they mean by Premier League proven? We aren’t getting Pep Guardiola or Jurgen Klopp!

What we would be getting is Premier League proven failures.

In a recent development, yes, let’s get Sean Dyche in. I can’t wait.

It has been revealed that yes, let’s get Rafa Benitez back and ruin all those great memories we have of how he stood by us at our moment of need. Rafa’s career has fallen off a cliff since NUFC and it would be horrific to see him come back and get abuse when he failed.

All managers have to start somewhere, only a very small handful of individuals who were stellar players then get gifted a top club in their first job as manager.

Matthias Jaissle has done well in Austria and Saudi Arabia.

Now he deserves a fair and proper chance in the Premier League, with Newcastle United.

Kanté – 5: Tried and failed to walk the ball into the net after the Portsmouth keeper fluffed his own punch from a corner. One lung-busting run early in the second half resulted in a half chance. Subbed for Castellanos 78′.

Now – familiar sinking feeling after conceding in the first half.

Austbø: : 6 Great chance to level it on 81 minutes, but his header was straight at the goalkeeper.

Magassa:  3  Two aimless overhit panic passes, playing as if it was the last minute.

According to one report, Liverpool have the opportunity to snap up a full-back from a fellow European giant for a modest amount.

The Reds have found a solution to the problematic right-back position with the loan acquisition of Ronald Araujo, who was originally signed to add centre-back cover but has excelled on the flank at Anfield.

Despite the Barcelona loanee’s fine form, Jamie Carragher has implored his former club to move for a full-back in January if the right opportunity arises, and there might just be another one from Camp Nou.

As reported by Graeme Bailey for TEAMtalk, the LaLiga champions are prepared to sanction an exit for Alejandro Balde amid interest from Liverpool, with Barca head coach Hansi Flick indicating that the 23-year-old isn’t part of his plans.

His representative Jorge Mendes has reportedly held talks with the Merseyside club to inform them of the conditions surrounding a potential deal for the player, who’s viewed by Anfield chiefs as an ‘attractive option’.

The agent is understood to have communicated a valuation of €40m (£33m) to prospective suitors, and that figure would apply whether the deal is structured as a permanent transfer or a loan arrangement with a purchase option.

Industry observers note that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Even though Balde has been overtaken by Xavi Espart and Joao Cancelo in the left-back pecking order at Barcelona, Liverpool might still feel that the price point apparently quoted by Mendes would represent something of a bargain for the 23-year-old.

Catalan columnist Javier Miguel has previously hailed some ‘spectacular’ performances from the Spain international (AS), and an analysis from The Athletic highlighted his aptitude for taking on opposition full-backs whilst marauding along the left flank.

He’s also renowned for his pace, with his former agent Junior Minguella describing him as a ‘bullet’, and Flick previously spoke of how the Spain international strives to ‘get better every day’ (The Athletic).

If Kostas Tsimikas were to depart at the end of his contract next summer – certainly not an implausible scenario – then Liverpool would need to add left-back competition for Milos Kerkez, and Barcelona’s apparent readiness to offload Balde could play into our hands.

Considering the success we’ve had so far with Araujo, FSG might just be inclined to sound out the Catalan giants about potentially adding another full-back option from Flick’s squad in 2027. This could be an intriguing one to watch over the coming months.

  • Didi Hamann signed for Newcastle United in 1998 from Bayern Munich.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Didi Hamann has been talking about Newcastle United.

Didi Hamann signed for Newcastle United in 1998 from Bayern Munich.

Kenny Dalglish the United manager who signed him for a reported £5.5m fee after the 1998 World Cup finals where he’d played for Germany.

Didi Hamann now giving his opinion on Newcastle United’s future stadium aims….

The former player turned pundit asked by Lottoland Live Casino: ‘Newcastle United are reportedly yet to decide whether to renovate or expand St James’ Park or build a completely new stadium. Do Newcastle United need a completely new stadium?’.

It has been revealed that didi Hamann replying: “No, no, you can’t leave St James’ Park. Obviously, I was fortunate and lucky to be able to play there for one season. I think it’s one of the best grounds in the league. With the extension they had, I think they get 51,000 [ED: 52k+ capacity now], and they probably can fit a few more in. If they can extend it, I think they’ve got to do everything to keep it. It’s right in the middle of the city. I think it’s one of the best, one of the most iconic stadia in the world. And I think this is why it would be majorly important to keep St James’. Don’t leave St James’ Park, please.”.

It is embarrassing that Didi Hamann is passing comment on this, considering how he was so desperate to leave St James’ Park less than a year after arriving and move to Liverpool.

The German international only started 20 Premier League matches for Newcastle United before forcing his way out of the club. In total he started 30 competitive games for United, plus one sub appearance. So fair to say he will have only started around 15 games in total at St James’ Park in a Newcastle United shirt.

The other thing when you are commenting on a club you don’t really care about, is that you also know precious little about the subject matter. If Didi Hamann had done his research then he would have known that there are zero looks to move the home of Newcastle United out of the city centre. That if indeed there is a fresh stadium built, then it will go up on a site no more than hundreds of yards away, very possibly even partly on the current St James’ Park site.

Industry observers note that the former (very short-term!) United star also asked: ‘Newcastle and Liverpool are both known for their incredible atmospheres. Having played at both grounds, which stadium do you think has the better atmosphere and where did you enjoy playing more?’.

Didi Hamann: “It’s very hard to compare because we didn’t play in Europe with Newcastle. Obviously, European nights at Anfield have always been special. But I’ve got to say, to walk out the first time at St James’ was just electric. When the music comes on, when you walk out and you see in my time, I think it was about 40, 45,000 Geordies [Ed: SJP capacity was 36k+ then] there. It was just fantastic. At the same time, I was in awe when I played with Newcastle the first time. I think it was Boxing Day that season in 1998 when we played Liverpool. When you stand in the tunnel there before it got redone. I think they are two of the best stadia in England. I’d go Premier League games at Newcastle, European nights at Anfield.”.

One Shot, One Goal, Three Points: West Ham’s Season in a Nutshell

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (644 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Claretandhugh

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After another disastrous result last night, I was left scratching my head wondering what can actually be done to solve the problems facing West Ham.
  • I think 50 points might be enough to survive this league!
  • Earlier this week I wrote about the statistics, and they tell the real story behind West Ham’s struggles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After another disastrous result last night, I was left scratching my head wondering what can actually be done to solve the problems facing West Ham. If results continue along this trajectory, the Hammers could find themselves looking nervously over their shoulders at the bottom end of the Championship table rather than fighting for promotion. At this rate, even a play-off spot feels optimistic.

I think 50 points might be enough to survive this league!

Earlier this week I wrote about the statistics, and they tell the real story behind West Ham’s struggles.

Shot after shot, chance after chance, attack after attack, and still the ball refuses to go in. Remarkably, despite their wastefulness, the Hammers remain the division’s top scorers. In the last two matches alone, they have struck the woodwork five times.

Against Portsmouth, West Ham registered 19 shots with six on target and failed to score.

Sources indicate that when you add that to the wider picture, the numbers become even more alarming. Across the last six matches, West Ham have taken 130 shots, with 41 on target, and scored only eight goals.

In a recent development, at the opposite end of the pitch, defensive frailties and questionable goalkeeping continue to cost the team. Herrick was barely tested at Fratton Park, but when he was called into action, he was beaten. The goal will almost certainly be recorded as a goalkeeping error. Portsmouth created virtually nothing, yet their only shot on target produced the winning goal.

In a recent development, you can only work with the players available, but it’s difficult to understand how Areola has suffered multiple injuries this season despite not playing a competitive match. Entering the final year of his contract, albeit with a club option for an additional season, he is reportedly earning around £60,000 per week.

These are issues that might be understandable in the Premier League. This is the Championship. These players, including the youngsters, should be capable of performing consistently at this level.

Heads – down, negativity growing…time to stop the rot….

The negativity around the club is beginning to grow.

Recent findings suggest that nuno had to go, and he did. His departure gave Parker an opportunity to reintegrate certain players and rebuild fitness levels through competitive football. To be fair, time has not always been on the fresh manager’s side. However, following the international break, he has now had a chance to work with the squad, implement his ideas and stamp his authority on the team.

Sources indicate that the last two matches have to fall at his door. One point from six is simply not good enough. Extend that across his first four games and the record reads two defeats and two draws.

The much-talked-about newly introduced manager bounce? It never arrived.

Industry observers note that you can see the frustration written all over the players’ faces. The supporters are becoming restless too, and I include myself in that group. I predicted a narrow 1-0 victory for West Ham at Portsmouth, but deep down I feared a repeat of the Preston performance. Unfortunately, those fears proved worse as at least we got a point on Saturday!

Recent findings suggest that against Preston, West Ham enjoyed 80% possession and recorded 53 touches inside the opposition penalty area. Preston registered just ten.

At Fratton Park, the Hammers dominated possession with 63% of the ball and managed 29 touches in Portsmouth’s box compared to just eight for the home side.

Recent findings suggest that at this point, I’m running out of explanations. The statistics suggest West Ham should be winning games comfortably, but football is decided by goals, not data. Right now, the Hammers can’t convert their dominance into results, and until that changes, the gap between expectation and reality will continue to grow. I’m lost for words. I really am!
