Ruben Amorim is not a coach who makes a habit of singling out individuals, but he made an exception in Saturday’s press conference.

As MilanNews recall, on the eve of the game against Frosinone, Amorim bluntly admitted that Christian Pulisic and Adrien Rabiot are the ‘irreplaceable’ players in the current squad. Their characteristics and their quality make them unique, in the eyes of the coach and many fans.

When the American and the Frenchman don’t play, the team’s fluidity and effectiveness suffer significantly. There is a stark contract between Milan when Rabiot and Pulisic play versus when both do not feature.

According to recent reports, amorim’s words were clear in his pre-match presser: “Every player appreciates having the club’s trust. And Pulisic’s upcoming contract has helped. When he wasn’t playing, I told you he was still crucial for Milan, and we can’t forget about the injured players.

“Pulisic is the only player we can’t replace today: the way he moves between the lines, we don’t have another Pulisic. In the last few European matches, we missed him; we had to manage him. If he’s not on the pitch, given his characteristics, you feel it.

It has been revealed that “And you understand how important he is. He doesn’t talk much, but he speaks a lot on the pitch with his play. He always wants the ball. He and Rabiot always lift the team up. I don’t like to talk about individuals, but I have to.

It has been revealed that “I think everyone can understand that. So Pulisic is our present, he will be our future, and I think he has the potential to do even more.”.

In a recent development, it’s worth noting that the coach emphasised the importance of Pulisic’s contract renewal too. This is also why the club are doing everything possible to reach an agreement for Rabiot.

It has been revealed that cardinale called him a top player and candidly admitted that he adores him, also emphasising how he respects his family. These statements are not coincidental, given that it is his mother who represents the midfielder.

According to recent reports, speaking of which, discussions with Véronique Rabiot are progressing positively. A meeting took place before the derby, which ended with a 3-1 win with a goal for the former Juventus and Marseille midfielder.

It has been revealed that the player is happy with the Rossoneri and wants to stay: a definitive agreement on the financial terms needs to be reached. Milan are also willing to adjust the player’s salary in order to secure him for a few more years at Milanello.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Inbetweeners at Newcastle United, can they become success stories this series (this season) and beyond.

So much could depend on how this quarter perform.

Just in case you weren’t aware, The Inbetweeners is a brilliant (in my opinion anyway) comedy series (that has also then produced a couple of excellent films).

This comedy is the story of four teenagers who are misfits, neither totally cool nor total outcasts (hence The Inbetweeners), who regularly find themselves in awkward situations of their own making,.

This fictional quartet occasionally hint of moving on to a consistently successful level, but their own inherent frailties as well as outside factors, time after time conspire to prevent those glimpses of promise becoming ever more than that.

My focus isn’t on individuals who have just arrived this summer at St James’ Park, it isn’t on young players, it isn’t on older players where we pretty much know what we are going to get.

When it comes to The Inbetweeners at Newcastle United, I wanted to concentrate on this quartet below.

Four players who have played plenty of Premier League football in their careers and have shown enough to suggest they COULD be crucial, indeed vital, for Newcastle United this season.

All four of them also happen to play in the key midfield and attacking positions, the positions where United need far higher input and productivity if they are to create the chances and score the goals that can make the (positive) difference this season.

So without further ado, here are The Inbetweeners at St James’ Park:.

I think that arguably he is THE ultimate Inbetweener at Newcastle United. He was brilliant in that 2022-23 fourth place finish season before then serious injury hit then fitness and form issues have followed.

At times we see THAT Joe Willock of 2022-23 and the second half on Saturday a prime example. Against his former club he was the key man in that second half,  the pressing of opposition players and his running with the ball, the Arsenal midfield couldn’t handle him at times. Willock pressured Odegaard into the mistake that produced the equaliser and then an assist for Thiaw’s strike.

Joe Willock would deserve to be first name on the team sheet if he consistently played like he did in that second half.

Started the season in electric form, confidence sky high as he scored within five minutes of the opening game against Liverpool, then in the first EPL away game scored a brilliant goal to set United on their way to beating Spurs.

It has been revealed that then injury hit and when he has returned, it feels a bit like Snakes and Ladders. He climbed plenty of ladders and got into a great position brimming with confidence, he then though hits one snake that sends his confidence and form sliding right back to rock bottom and needing to start again.

Sources indicate that I bit like Willock and Saturday’s second half, Elanga needs to simply get his head back in the place it was when Liverpool and Spurs couldn’t handle him. He is capable of being a huge player for Matthias Jaissle AND he needs to be that player to solve our problem on the right. He did alright on Saturday when he came on and maybe a huge factor can be if Tino Livramento now can stay fit as well on that side.

Very similar story to Anthony Elanga, started this season on fire and then lost his way.

In certain moments, Yoane Wissa has looked unplayable (in a good way!) this season, some of his runs on the ball have been exhilarating. The one he made with a handful of Liverpool players challenging him half the length of the pitch before passing to Joe Willock for his goal, where has that gone?

Again like Elanga, with Wissa it feels like it is very much a confidence thing.

Industry observers note that he had an astonishing record at Brentford but I do feel he is an attacker who is more of a team player, he needs those around him also playing well. Hopefully if the team overall can become more consistent and then Yoane Wissa finds within that some special moments of his own, we can just maybe have that opening of this season player back again.

Of this quartet of Inbetweeners at Newcastle United, I think Ramsey deserves to be cut the most slack.

The former Villa star has still only started 15 Premier League matches for Newcastle United and was very unlucky with a bad early injury last season (thanks to Sean Longstaff) and desperately needs a run in the team to get his rhythm after having his own struggles with fitness and form.

In a recent development, like the other three above, Jacob Ramsey has had moments where we can see the player Eddie Howe signed. The same as Joe Willock, Ramsey is very mobile, runs well with the ball, can be very effective with a high press, can be a difference maker.

The second half on Saturday he showed that and I do think that if Newcastle United are to exceed any current expectations, we need to have players with pace who can swiftly carry the ball in transition an cause problems for opposition teams on a regular basis. If Jacob Ramsey and Joe Willock can do it against the best team in the country, admittedly just for one half on Saturday, why can’t they do it against the rest?

Once again though, the same as Yoane Wissa and Anthony Elanga, it is all about this quarter losing their status as The Inbetweeners at Newcastle United and proving to be something far better than that.

Here’s hoping they prove they are worthy of another series.

Scott Parker could do little else other than state the obvious last night as West Ham plumbed new depths of mediocrity against their south coast opponents. For the first time this season, the league’s top scorers failed to find their opponent’s net despite again hitting the woodwork twice.

Speaking after the game, Parker came up with a newly introduced expression for ‘pulling their finger out’ – when speaking to West Ham tv:.

“We need to fix up as a group and as a team and give ourselves a platform.”.

Sources indicate that this is an honest group. They’re probably too desperate, really and I think that’s weighing quite heavy and you can see that.

It has been revealed that it’s just certain moments we’re a little bit soft in certain moments. We’re easy to play against in certain moments.”.

Sources indicate that which means, as we can all see for ourselves it is less about the quality of the play, more about the mental resilience of the eleven on the pitch who have seemingly lost – for the time being – the ability to take another low blow and fight back. Conceding one goal away at Portsmouth is no disaster. Failing to register two goals against them is the real failing.

Another year, another hit: Soucek’s commitment to this team stands head, shoulders, torso and boots above some within the limp lettuce line up. Right now it ss more about the character of those selected than the ability.

According to recent reports, at times earlier in the season West Ham would have romped down the other end and banged in three in quick succession to redress the balance and grab the points. And that is what Parker needs to find again. It isn’t the magic fix of a ‘perfect’ defensive performance, our players aren’t good enough to give us that. It is a mental resilience that ten didn’t have last night.

Eleven Tomas Souceks, players who are prepared to bleed for this club, will do nicely.

Clearly some ( c’mon, we know who they are) aren’t prepared to dig in, to battle, to die for the shirt ( metaphorically speaking of course) ands they’re the ones who need to be sidelined. Forget the (huh) best footballers. Give us 10 fighters alongside Soucek.

It has been revealed that the Czech showed again why, without being the best footballer, he wins the admiration of every West Ham fan. Because he bleeds for the team. The rest would do well to follow his example.

Back in July, Kyle Healy-Matthews was tempted away from West Ham by Newcastle United.

The highly teenage starlet was a young player the Hammers were desperate not to lose.

Newcastle United fighting off a number of other Premier League clubs who had been competing to attract the teenage right-back.

However, personal terms were agreed between NUFC and Kyle Healy-Matthews and the deal completed.

Obviously one for the future he looked a very positive addition, the young right-back is quick and with very good defensive ability, he’d been a stand out player in the West Ham young set-up.

Since the October 2021 takeover, Newcastle United having signed a lot of promising young players from other clubs, which will hopefully pay longer-term benefits.

Now Newcastle United have revealed on Wednesday morning that Kyle Healy-Matthews has signed his first professional contract with the club on his 17th birthday.

Official Newcastle United media stating: ‘The Romford-born youngster joined Newcastle’s Academy from West Ham United last summer and initially linked up with Chris Moore’s Under-18s squad as a first-year scholar before agreeing professional terms with the Magpies. Healy-Matthews, who primarily plays as a right-back, expressed his delight in committing his future with Newcastle and has relished his time at United’s Little Benton Academy to date.’.

According to recent reports, kyle Healy-Matthews: “I’m very pleased to sign my first professional contract,” he told newcastleunited.com. “It’s a special moment for myself and my family, seeing all the hard work which has led up to this. Newcastle is a massive club with goals and ambitions that I feel I can contribute in. I believe I can play a substantial part for this club. I’ve enjoyed my time here a lot. I’ve had a lot of support from my peers and coaches with helping me to settle in as well as progressing along the way.”.

In a recent development, the official NUFC media going on to say: ‘Kyle Healy-Matthews, who cites fellow right-back Kyle Walker as his footballing idol, has made a positive start to the current campaign at Under-18 level, with the Toon teenagers winning six of their opening seven league matches and right now occupying third spot in the division. The rapid full-back believes he has handled the challenge of relocating hundreds of miles away from home for the first time and is determined to advance through the Magpies’ youth ranks. Healy-Matthews, a member of West Ham’s Under-17 Premier League Cup winning side last season.’.

According to recent reports, kyle Healy-Matthews: “I’ve only been here for a few months but I think I can say the move has paid off. Moving very far away from home could have been tricky but with all of the support I had around me from my peers, that really helped me to settle in rapidly. I’m loving my time with the Under-18s. This season, my main aim is to progress into the Under-21s and long-term, but hopefully not too long, would be to progress into the first-team.”.

Steve Harper is Newcastle United Academy Director: “Kyle has made an excellent impression since joining the Academy in the summer and we’re pleased to see him rewarded with his first professional contract. Moving away from home and settling into a upcoming environment can be a significant challenge for any young player but Kyle has handled the transition brilliantly. He’s worked extremely hard since arriving at the club and his attitude, commitment and willingness to learn have stood out throughout his time here so far. This contract is recognition of the progress he’s made, and we’re excited to continue supporting his development as he takes the next steps in his career at Newcastle United.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With only two points from his first four games, West Ham manager Scott Parker is already coming under pressure, with some even questioning whether he is the right man to take the club forward following last night’s defeat at Portsmouth.

In a recent development, for me, it’s a little premature to be discussing the upcoming manager’s job security. But make no mistake about it, West Ham are a club in crisis, and there is a lot more wrong than just the manager.

In a recent development, however, the one thing Parker can control is how he utilises the players at his disposal. And from my seat in Row B at Fratton Park, it was evident that Parker appears no closer to knowing what his best starting XI is.

Problems in both full-back positions, a lack of creativity through the middle, genuine issues on the left wing and three strikers who can’t score goals.

West Ham huffed and puffed against Pompey, and no doubt the statistics will have been boosted by a late flurry towards the end of the game when we battered the Portsmouth goal for five minutes. But that could not disguise the fact that we were watching a very, very poor West Ham team.

I had a close-up view of West Ham hams problems from row B at Fratton Park.

Possibly the most disturbing aspect is that neither Preston North End nor Portsmouth, in our last two games, have looked like particularly good teams. The fact of the matter is that you don’t have to be a decent side to beat West Ham.

We now find ourselves closer to the relegation places than automatic promotion, and I’ve seen little to suggest that anyone knows how to turn us around and get us pointing in the right direction.

There’s a massive game coming up at the London Stadium against Stoke City, but make no mistake about it, the Potters will be licking their lips at the prospect of turning over West Ham.

The Hammers are now starting to look less like promotion certainties and more like Leicester City.

Hexa-substituted benzene synthesis with non-classical carbocations

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (469 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, benzene rings are the most frequently encountered ring system in small-molecule drugs1.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, benzene rings are the most frequently encountered ring system in small-molecule drugs1. However, benzenes with six substituents are notably absent from small molecule libraries, owing to challenges associated with their synthesis and the limited availability of commercially available aromatic building blocks2. Therefore, new chemical processes that enable their synthesis with predictable regiochemical control and broad substituent diversity could enable medicinal chemists to explore this uncharted aromatic chemical space in hit-to-lead and lead optimization campaigns. Herein, we describe a highly modular and programmable platform for accessing hexa-substituted benzene rings from aromatic cyclopropenium cations and (trialkylsilyl)allenes, with precise control over all six benzene positions encoded in the starting materials. The exceptional regioselectivity observed originates from the selective evolution of an unusual non-classical carbocation featuring four-centre four-electron bonding as revealed by density functional theory calculations. Our benzannulation enables the selective installation of synthetic handles that were exploited for the synthesis of previously inaccessible penta- and hexa-substituted analogues of the anticancer drug sonidegib and the antihypertensive drug telmisartan, as well as the polyaromatic hydrocarbon triphenylene. Notably, the use of enantiopure allenes unlocks a new route to enantioenriched multi-substituted biaryls through our benzannulation occurring with “memory of chirality”.

Recent findings suggest that there’s talk, behind the scenes, at West Ham regarding the Nuno era that came before and the differences that’ve taken hold under latest coach Scott Parker. If anything, on the pitch West Ham have got worse under their former player-turned-head-coach as the slide down the second division continues.

Even with former Hammers legend Mark Noble on the coaching staff, the players look lost and at times without fight or character. Which comes as a shock to supporters who had expected the opposite would be the case with the hugely popular duo at the helm.

In a recent development, as footballers they excelled – but they’re being tested like never before. They still deserve the fans’ support. In my humble opinion. Disagree? Go for it, That’s what we have a ‘comments’ section for.

However, the talk is, apparently, not all doom and gloom.

TalkSPORT’ sAlex Crook, reporting during the Portsmouth v West Ham game, claimed his own exclusive:.

“I was speaking to a couple of West Ham staff and they were saying, even if the results aren’t coming, the general atmosphere is a lot better than it was under Nuno.”.

According to recent reports, if that is the case and there’s progress off the pitch then we as fans will just have to suck it up and get behind this group. They’re the only 26 available until January and whilst they aren’t very good, the majority are at least, trying.

Noble and Parker have to pick the eleven who will try their hearts out and run over hot coals for their manager and their supporters.

At least then the players won’t hang back for fear of being abused amidst away-end ‘ugly scenes‘ after the final whistle as the BBC reported.

Recent findings suggest that that surely has to stop, however frustrated supporters feel. It won’t make the players perform any better. The opposite, in fact.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Barcelona sporting director Deco has left the door wide open for Liverpool to sign Ronald Araujo permanently.

The Uruguayan joined the Reds on a season-long loan in August and has made an immediate impression on the Anfield faithful, putting in a series of tremendous performances at right-back for Andoni Iraola’s side.

Reports from Spain in recent days have indicated that Merseyside chiefs are keen to take up the option to sign the defender outright for £47m, with the player also understood to be ready to stay in L4 beyond next summer.

Liverpool’s chances of securing him on a permanent basis would appear to have been greatly boosted by comments from Deco.

The Barcelona chief told Catalunya Radio’s Tot Costa: “A bit of money wouldn’t hurt us either. We’d be happy because things have gone well, and we’d be happy for him too.

Industry observers note that “Personally, I’m happy for Ronald. He’s one of the team’s leaders. He’s been through some difficult times and some happy ones at the club, and we have a good relationship.

“He’s made his decision, and we respect it. The most important thing for us is to see him happy. If he decides to stay and things carry on like this, we’d be happy with that too.”.

(Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images).

Recent findings suggest that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

It seems that, if Liverpool were to sign Araujo permanently, everyone would be a winner.

The Reds would secure a player who’s been excellent for them (and get a deal done at a relatively modest fee), the defender would get to remain on Merseyside (where his family are reportedly very happy), and Barcelona would bank nearly £50m for someone they’re seemingly happy to let go.

Even with Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni finally back in first-team training, both of them will realistically need a few more weeks to be properly matchday ready, so Iraola will continue to depend heavily on the Uruguayan to maintain form and fitness.

Liverpool won’t be able to activate the purchase option on Araujo until the end of the season, and it’s not implausible that he could succumb to a serious injury or see his performance levels drop in the meantime.

Right now, though, there’s no excuse for Anfield chiefs not to go all-out to secure a permanent transfer, especially with Deco indicating that Barcelona would be prepared to sanction his sale. Don’t fumble this one please, Julian Ward!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Graham Scott has been quizzed by an Arsenal fan as to why Malick Thiaw’s goal was allowed to stand on Saturday.
  • That goal put Newcastle United 2-1 up on 62 minutes.
  • Graham Scott refereed in the Premier League for a decade and he was also a video assistant referee (VAR) more than 100 times.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Graham Scott has been quizzed by an Arsenal fan as to why Malick Thiaw’s goal was allowed to stand on Saturday.

That goal put Newcastle United 2-1 up on 62 minutes.

Graham Scott refereed in the Premier League for a decade and he was also a video assistant referee (VAR) more than 100 times.

Now retired, he brings his unique insight into how match officials operate for The Athletic.

They invite readers to send in questions each week for Graham Scott to answer.

This week the former top referee received this one from an Arsenal fan….

‘Why did neither the referee nor VAR penalise the holding on Jurrien Timber that allowed Dan Burn to win a free header to create Newcastle’s second goal against Arsenal?’.

According to recent reports, graham Scott explaining: “Timber was impeded by Will Osula as he chased after Burn (circled below). Osula was impeded by Declan Rice, who was holding him with both arms. Malick Thiaw was being held by Martin Odegaard, who was being held by Thiaw. Lewis Miley blocked Ezri Konsa, who pulled Miley to get past him. There were probably other potential fouls, too. The officials look for the most serious offences that have the greatest impact, and none of these came close to meeting those thresholds — which are set by the league and the lawmakers, not the refs.”.

I know that no football fan takes it well when any decision goes against them BUT as a group I think Arsenal fans do appear especially bizarre in terms of not willing to accept any decision that doesn’t go their way.

Graham Scott was also asked another question regarding Saturday’s game….

‘When David Raya went down for treatment the first time at Newcastle on Saturday, why did another Arsenal player not have to leave the field for a minute? I thought that was the fresh rule.’.

Graham Scott: ‘No Arsenal player was asked to leave the field for a minute because Raya had collided with an opponent and requested treatment at the earliest opportunity. There is a similar exemption if a goalkeeper’s injury occurs from a foul that the referee deems worthy of a yellow or red card. This rule was introduced to stop goalkeepers mysteriously sitting down and demanding treatment for fictitious muscle injuries while their coach held an impromptu time-out chat with the rest of the team.’.

In a recent development, I have to confess, I totally forgot about this fresh rule coming in. Has any goalkeeper got ‘injured’ this season and had treatment on the pitch which led to his Premier League side going down to ten men for a minute with an outfield player going off?

On the face of it West Ham have too few options in key areas of the pitch, meaning that despite their ineffectiveness, the same payers have to be utilised again and again.

Joel Piroe, after another anonymous evening, will probably get selected to start at Saturday simply because of the options available: Neither Taty Castellanos who was invisible in his 10 minutes last night nor Pablo Felipe who is not even making Parker’s squad offer a better option as potential goal scorers. So Piroe’s ineffectiveness is set to continue.

The same applies in the case of  right back Joel Veltman: Albeit through Kyle Walker Peters‘ injury, Scott Parker has very little option but to start the Dutchman again, despite his pretty universally condemned performance at Fratton Park.

Veltman- unable to add much to West Ham’s offensive capabilities.

Footballfancast.com  single out Veltman for special mention:.

“The Dutchman, who is averaging 0.5 key passes and 0.1 dribbles per game, was once again ineffective in possession against Portsmouth before being substituted in the 62nd minute.

Veltman has never produced more than three assists in a season in his career and has not assisted more than one league goal in a season since the 2016/17 campaign with Ajax, which shows that he is an even bigger problem [than Piroe] as he does not have relevant experience to suggest that he will turn things around.

Parker must, now, drop the defender to the bench to explore his options in that area of the pitch, as the Hammers need more on the ball from the player in that position moving forward.”.

Industry observers note that can’t really argue with that but unless Scott Parker is prepared to start Arne Engels as an emergency right back then the Hammers boss is fresh out of options until Walker Peters recovers. Veltman was the free signing designed to give West Ham cover in the event of injury. We’d not perhaps envisaged him being required to play week in, week out. His failure going forward is likely the reason Jarrod Bowen is having to play so wide.

Just an observation but does seem a trend when Walker Peters is absent, that Bowen hugs the touch line more, knowing his full back is not going to overlap or assist him in the way in which Walker Peters can.

Time, then, for anxious glances to the treatment table to see how Walker Peter’s recuperation from his thigh muscle glitch is going.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Breaking news on Wednesday that the Saudi Arabia PIF have put 25 per cent of Newcastle United up for sale.
  • The exclusive comes from David Ornstein and Chris Waugh at The Athletic.
  • They reveal that this would be done through the issuing of new shares.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Breaking news on Wednesday that the Saudi Arabia PIF have put 25 per cent of Newcastle United up for sale.

The exclusive comes from David Ornstein and Chris Waugh at The Athletic.

They reveal that this would be done through the issuing of new shares.

The Athletic stating: ‘The proposed transaction would see fresh investors inject funds directly into the club, receiving up to a quarter shareholding in exchange. No funds would flow to PIF, but its existing stake would be diluted by the share issue.’.

They add that JP Morgan (the Latest York City-headquartered global bank) has been appointed advisors and that the process to find investment is under way.

The Athletic journalists detailing: ‘Sources with knowledge of the situation, speaking on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to do so publicly, insisted that, at this point, a minority investor is being sought with PIF eager to raise money, in part to fund major infrastructure projects, and regard the issuing of new shares as a good means of doing so.’.

It appears that the 25 per cent of the total shareholding to be sold will come from the 84 per cent of the club owned by the Saudi Arabia PIF, as the report adds that: ‘The British Reuben family owns the remaining 16 per cent shareholding and Jamie Reuben is their representative on the board.’.

Back in May 2026, The Athletic had previously reported that the Newcastle United majority owners were open to selling a minority stake to help fund significant infrastructure projects: ‘However, people familiar with the matter insisted PIF retained a long-term commitment to the club they jointly bought from Mike Ashley for a total of £305million ($400.1m at present exchange rates) in 2021, though they were willing to dilute their shareholding and had already been approached by possible investors. Yasir Al-Rumayyan, PIF’s governor and Newcastle’s chairman, attended his first match of the season at St James’ Park on Saturday, watching Newcastle draw 2-2 with league champions Arsenal. Jamie Reuben was also at the match.’.

This news today will hopefully signal looks for the upcoming stadium set to finally go head, as well as the new state of the art training ground.

The Athletic adding: ‘While PIF was never going to pay for a fresh stadium outright — Newcastle have always been viewed as a long-term investment intended to bring them an eventual profit — any project of that scale would require a notable injection of equity as well as outside financing.’.

In recent years Aston Villa getting into the Champions League not once, but twice, for the first time in decades (since the days it was called the European Cup).

The two clubs with proud histories also have another far bigger thing in common.

They are by far and away the two disruptor Premier League clubs, the pair who have tried hardest to break the modern day ‘Major Six’ financial stranglehold on long-term power and success.

Aston Villa and Newcastle United have flown closest to the Sun and suffered because of it, with UEFA SCR restrictions battering them into submission. If you don’t follow their warnings and get back in financial check, then face a ban from the Champions League (and other UEFA competitions) in the future.

It is all part of the endless vicious circle for clubs such as Aston Villa and Newcastle United who are attempting to narrow that yawning financial chasm that exists between themselves and the ‘Premier League Big Six’ who have been allowed to build such seemingly unchallengeable financial powerhouses across many years when Mike Ashley ran United into the ground and Villa suffered in many ways of their own.

This is the Champions League story of recent years for Aston Villa and Newcastle United.

2022-23 season Newcastle United qualify for next season’s Champions League but Aston Villa don’t.

Industry observers note that 2023-24 season Newcastle United compete in that season’s Champions League but Aston Villa don’t. Aston Villa qualify for next season’s Champions League but Newcastle United don’t.

2024-25 season Aston Villa compete in that season’s Champions League but Newcastle United don’t. Newcastle United qualify for next season’s Champions League but Aston Villa don’t.

Sources indicate that 2025-26 season Newcastle United compete in that season’s Champions League but Aston Villa don’t. Aston Villa qualify for next season’s Champions League but Newcastle United don’t.

2026-27 season Aston Villa compete in that season’s Champions League but Newcastle United don’t. Qualifying for…Aston Villa??? Newcastle United???

2026-27 season Competing/Qualifying for…Aston Villa??? Newcastle United???

The pattern couldn’t be clearer for Aston Villa and Newcastle United in recent years.

An ability every other year to qualify for the Champions League BUT in years when playing in the top European competition, unable to also qualify for the following season’s Champions League.

Recent findings suggest that four seasons in a row we have had either Newcastle United or Aston Villa disrupting the route of Premier League Big Six clubs to the Champions League BUT from where I am standing, it looks like that run is going to end now. I find it very unlikely that either Aston Villa or Newcastle United will qualify via the Premier League.

I think that now things have well and truly caught up with the two clubs and their ambitions.

I think to properly stand a chance of having a season where you can compete in the Champions League and attempt to qualify via the Premier League for the following season’s UCL competition, you need to have a squad with enough quality and depth to cope.

The financial rules make this all but impossible for Aston Villa and Newcastle United as things stand.

It has been revealed that wages are the most crippling thing, the Premier League Massive Six are able to pay far bogger wages than Newcastle United and Aston Villa. It reaches a point where they can’t pay their star plays anything close to the market rate (what they can get elsewhere). It also means that to try and somehow have a large enough squad to cope with both Premier League and Champions League, you need to sells some/all of your best players so you can afford to bring in enough signings to try and give you the depth.

Recent findings suggest that the reality in recent years when Aston Villa and Newcastle United have been trying to do both, compete in the Champions League AND qualify for next season’s, they have to play their small group of very best players far too often. This all but guarantees these star players will pick up injuries and/or get fatigued and their effectiveness is vastly diminished.

Photo by Jamie Smith via The Mag.

I think the perfect storm has now arrived.

All of the above issues have been impacted by the Premier League PSR and now SCR restrictions BUT even more so by the far stricter UEFA SCR restrictions on allowed spending on transfer fees and wages as a proportion of your revenues (UEFA allows 70% of ‘Adjusted operating revenue’).

I know that as football fans (especially those of Newcastle United and Aston Villa) we are heartily sick of all the accountancy boring side of things and how it constantly impacts the coverage of Premier League clubs these days.

To simply spell it out though, it basically means that if your revenues are twice as big as another club’s, you can spend twice as much on wages and transfer fees.

Roughly speaking, the likes of Arsenal, Liverpool, Man City and Man U have twice as substantial revenues as Aston Villa and Newcastle United have per season, whilst Chelsea and Tottenham are also way ahead AND have various other elements that give them an inbuilt advantage, which has been put in place across many years.

This past summer transfer window, in order to comply with UEFA SCR restrictions and avoid a future ban on taking part in UEFA competitions, both Villa and Newcastle had to take drastic action when it came to buying and selling players AND their wage bills.

It would have been unrealistic and reckless this summer for a club like Villa or Newcastle to agree to long-term huge wages of a level that ‘Massive Six’ clubs can comfortably afford.

Sources indicate that you then have Newcastle United and Aston Villa also having to sell at least some of their best players because they generally bring in the biggest instant benefit to a club’s accounts. The transfer fee agreed (less the player’s current book value) all goes into that current season’s accounts as a profit. However, when a player is bought the transfer fee that is agreed is spread over the length of his contract, when it comes to showing as a cost in the annual accounts. So if you sign a player for £50m on a five year contract, each season it indicates as a £10m cost in the accounts. So basically if you sell a player for a major transfer fee it can help you afford a number of players for a total higher than that transfer fee BUT they still eventually have to be accounted for. Plus of course all Premier League clubs are constantly having those annual transfer fee costs for previous signings going into the accounts.

So what did Aston Villa and Newcastle United do in summer 2026?

Or rather, what did they HAVE to do?

According to recent reports, they both sold a lot of their best and highest paid players to other clubs. In general, these players went to clubs who paid them far higher wages. Then Villa and Newcastle generally recruited players on lower transfer fees, many of who they also hope will improve in terms of value as well as ability in years to come.

Newcastle United lost the likes of Gordon, Trippier, Bruno and Tonali, having previously had to sell Isak and sacrifice Minteh and Anderson as well.

As well as previous players they had been forced to trade, this summer Aston Villa moved on the likes of Rogers, Watkins, Martinez, Digne, Konsa and Tielemans.

Interesting to see where many of these players are now at:.

Bruno (Arsenal), Rogers (Chelsea), Isak (Liverpool), Tielemans (Man U), Tonali (Tottenham), Martinez (Chelsea), Anderson (Man City), Konsa (Arsenal)….

So not only are Aston Villa and Newcastle United forced to move on many of their best players in order to stay inside the UEFA and EPL SCR restrictions, they then see most of them end up at the very Premier League Big Six clubs that they are trying to compete with, against the odds.

When it comes to power and success long-term, it feels very much like tossing a coin and it is heads the Premier League Big Six win, whilst tails sees Villa and Newcastle lose.

Aston Villa and Newcastle United presently sit 12th and 13th in the Premier League table, from 11 attempts each they have won three EPL matches apiece.

Where might the pair have been instead if the financial restrictions didn’t leave them hamstrung?

What if they weren’t prevented from matching the wages that Premier League Big Six clubs are able to pay, were able to keep all of their best players AND bring in similar quality ones that would help persuade them to stay AND enable them to properly compete long-term?

The contract with Adidas – which will begin in the summer of 2028 – is quite a sensational deal for the industry and for the club’s final years in terms of sporting results. It will bring in €50m per season for 10 seasons, the highest in Serie A by some margin.

In a recent development, bruno Fernandes is another name to keep an eye on. The Manchester United captain left Italy many years ago as a promising youngster and now wants to return as a top player. The Portuguese is a possible candidate, even if he is currently twinned with Nike.

It has been revealed that last but not least – in terms of consideration and feasibility – is Real Madrid’s Endrick. Milan are ready to make him one of the symbols of their latest project and have a bid of €60m plus bonuses ready to try to break down Los Blancos’ wall.

Sources indicate that jose Mourinho is the main obstacle between the Rossoneri and the Brazilian star, but Cardinale is unwavering and ready to do everything possible to bring him to Milanello as early as January. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Watching last night’s woeful performance against Portsmouth unfold, I was struck by the similarity in playing style of one current West Ham winger with a previous playing enigma from whom West Ham could never seem to coax the best.

Triggered by the  irritation generated from watching Manor Solomon constantly check back, slow down play and then inevitably cut inside, I found myself comparing him with another West Ham winger who repeated the same trick ad nauseam.

Even on the one occasion when he was put clean through beyond his full back, by a brilliant pass from Ezra Mayers, Solomon got to the by line and – infuriatingly, checked back instead of trying to cross with his weaker foot.

And at that moment I thought “Saïd Benrahma” all over again.

The enigma that was Saîd Benrahma: at least he scored a few, created a few, and smacked a mean penalty past Fiorentina’s keeper in the summer of 2023.

‘Benny’ could at least create chances (and score a mean penalty) whereas Manor Solomon just runs down blind alleys, head down, inevitably slowing and cutting inside to use his right foot.

It has been revealed that exactly as, on numerous occasions in each game, the Algerian would check back, infuriatingly, and slow up play instead of pressing on to beat his full back on the inside or out. In that respect Solomon seems identical, disrupting West Ham’s flow, allowing defenders to reset and frustrating the bejesus out of supporters.

At least Benrahma could create and occasionally score: Solomon has, by the reckoning of westhamworld.co.uk, now played “1141 minutes for two goals and two assists, averaging a goal every 285 minutes”.

For whatever reason the Israeli clearly is a shadow of the player who helped fire Leeds to promotion and West Ham need to consign him to the same ‘rest and recuperation’ home in which Mads Hermansen has been sent to recapture his form.

Austbo at least has a shot on him and seems to be able to beat players inside and out: With the Norwegian there is the feeling that there’s more to come. With Solomon, exactly as Tottenham fans suggested, the fear is that his best days are long in the rear view mirror. Much like Saîd Benrahma, but without the trophy to show for it.

It has now been revealed what each of the 20 Premier League clubs received from the 2025-26 TV cash payouts.

The information made public via the publication of the EPL’s official 2025-26 annual report.

This report including a breakdown of how much money each of last season’s 20 Premier League clubs banked.

In total, the 20 Premier League clubs received £3,142m for the 2025-26 season.

This is a 10.9% increase on the 2024-25 season.

Banking the most were Arsenal with £198.1m, whilst Wolves received the least with £117.2m.

Sources indicate that the Premier League is actually one of the very fairest major European leagues in terms of the gap between which clubs get the very most and very least. Arsenal getting 1.69 x what Wolves received.

This is the breakdown of the total distributions of £3,142m between the 20 Premier League clubs (in order of placings in the Premier League table for the 2025-26 season):.

£198.1m Arsenal £192.7m Man City £191.3m Man U £182.1m Aston Villa £181.6m Liverpool £170.2m Bournemouth £167.7m Sunderland £161.7m Brighton £160.8m Brentford £163.4m Chelsea £154.5m Fulham £153.7m Newcastle United £147.1m Everton £144.2m Leeds £136.4m Palace £135.9 Forest £136.6m Spurs £127.9m West Ham £118.6m Burnley £117.2m Wolves.

As you can see, some clubs got more than one or more of those that finished above them in the table. This is due to how many times the relative clubs were chosen for live UK coverage, this is the ‘Facility Fees’ portion of the cash.

The Newcastle United total of £153.7m is broken down as:.

UNITED KINGDOM (VIA THE TV DEALS ETC.) Equal Share £31.9m Facility Fees £20.3m Merit £15.4m.

CENTRAL COMMERCIAL Equal Share £11.2m.

OVERSEAS (VIA THE TV DEALS ETC.) Equal Share £56.5m Merit £18.4m.

Sources indicate that newcastle United received £6.5m less than 2024-25 as they fell eight places in the Premier League table. However, it would have been a far bigger drop without the overall 10.9% increase in the entire share out and the fact that NUFC were selected 31 times for UK TV coverage across 2025-26.

AC Milan resume their Serie A campaign after the final international break on 2026 by welcoming Frosinone to San Siro.

Ruben Amorim’s side are in need of a win to climb back into the top four after Como’s result on Saturday, while Roma and Lazio also picked up victories. They face a Frosinone team who will be full of confidence after an excellent start to their campaign, following promotion in 2025-26.

The latest team news suggests that Amorim will go with a 4-4-1-1 formation, though in his pre-match press conference he did not give too much away about his selection choices, especially in view of Thursday’s trip to Greece.

Sources indicate that at the risk of sounding like a broken record, something simply has to click for Goncalo Ramos, and preferably soon. He has gone one month without a goal and his struggles to even generate shots followed him to Portugal on international duty. However, Frosinone are a side that score goals but also let them in too, so there should be spaces to exploit.

In a recent development, it will be an intriguing battle between the No.9 and Gabriele Calvani, while it could even be an audition of sorts for the centre-back. Milan have been linked with the Genoa loanee, who has made an impressive start to the campaign, so it will be an up-close look as he tries to pile the misery on Ramos.

According to recent reports, with top scorer Antonio Raimondo out injured, Giorgi Kvernadze will be the main goal threat for the away side. The Georgian’s seven goal contributions are only bettered by the Italian striker, and he has started all 11 games under Alvini so far in Serie A.

It seems that Mario Gila will be tasked with stopping Kvernadze. The Spaniard spent the break at Milanello after not being called up by Spain again, and he should slot in as the right-sided defender again next to Koni De Winter.

Moving into midfield, there will be a fascinating contest between Adrien Rabiot and Giacomo Calo. It starts with a very obvious point of comparison: both are known for their goal scoring prowess, with the Frenchman already on five for the season and the Italian having racked up the same number.

The pair are likely to face each other head-to-head too. Whereas Rabiot has usually played deeper like Calo, it seems that the head coach is thinking of moving him further forward to play behind Ramos, so he will see a lot of Calo and also Patrizio Masini.

In a recent development, alvini is expected to give the nod to Aleksa Terzic at left-back, which is notable because the Serbian has only started one game so far in 2026-27, with his other four appearances all coming off the bench. He does like to get forward in transition though, and has a goal to his name.

According to recent reports, primarily, Terzic will be tasked with trying to limit Diego Moreira’s impact on the game. The Belgian – who scored for his national team for the first time in their rout of Italy – is expected to start on the right for the Rossoneri, and his seven goal contributions in seven games tell their own story.

Industry observers note that finally, we return to the middle of the park where Luka Modric and Romano Schmid will headline as series of interesting duels. Modric’s importance to Milan in all phases of the game have been written about at length, but particularly the build-up phase in games where his team are expected to dominate the ball.

The Croatian is the metronome for the Rossoneri just as the summer signing Schmid is for the Canarini. The Austrian has been playing mostly as an attacking midfielder, with two goals and four assists to his name, and starts in all 11 rounds thus far.

  • Published: 10:52 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:13 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Rangers boss Derek McInnes insists the incentive of next month's Premier Sports Cup Final can fuel his players as they prepare to embark on a vital run of fixtures.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 10:52 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:13 EST, 23 November 2026.

Rangers boss Derek McInnes insists the incentive of next month's Premier Sports Cup Final can fuel his players as they prepare to embark on a vital run of fixtures.

A 2-1 triumph over Motherwell on Saturday night stretched Rangers' unbeaten run to 13 matches after Ryan Naderi struck a late winner at Fir Park.

McInnes' side will host a revitalised Aberdeen at Ibrox on Tuesday night, before two further home matches against Falkirk and Dundee United over the next week.

They will then face a double-header against Hibs, with a league clash at Easter Road swiftly followed by the cup final.

McInnes insists no player is guaranteed their place in the team - and challenged them to earn their place for the Hampden showpiece as they look to win the first trophy of the season.

Recent findings suggest that 'I think the squad looks strong at the minute,' stated the Ibrox boss. 'We've got good options and good options from the bench to turn to.

Derek McInnes has led Rangers on a 13-game unbeaten run in all competitions.

'In this little run of fixtures, hopefully everybody will start to play a wee bit more of their part and hopefully more winning performances.

'I don't think I'll mention it [the cup final] too often, but they are not daft, they see that and everybody wants to play in the team.

'Anybody who's in the team needs to keep playing well to stay in the team and anybody who's not in the team needs to train right and take advantage of their minutes.

Sources indicate that 'We make that point often enough. Sometimes you've got to go away to tough venues like Motherwell and do the hard work and get the reward.

'But there's bigger games, more games like cup finals to take part in, so everybody wants to play in that one.

'I'm sure it does us no harm. I think it keeps the fans bubbling along, a chance of silverware, so when it comes along hopefully, as I say, we're in good form.'.

Rangers are on a strong run of form and haven't lost a game since they were dumped out of Europe against Jablonec at the end of August.

The victory over Motherwell maintained their position in second in the table, four points adrift of Celtic with a game in hand.

Up against an Aberdeen side buoyed by their first win under new boss Mario Frick at the weekend, McInnes wants his players to keep the pedal to the metal.

'I think it's unusual with five games now away from Ibrox, four in the league and the cup game, and now the fixtures kind of run the other way,' stated the Rangers boss.

'We've got some good fixtures at home but I think we always look at little blocks in the weeks, and where we're looking to try and get to by a certain period, and get certain points and certain targets.

Sources indicate that 'But first thing's first now with Aberdeen. We've got to make sure we're a strong home team again. Hopefully we can score a few more goals but, ultimately, as long as we win the game, I'll be happy.

'I think there's always a wee concern when you've got so many away on an international break, but obviously now with the January break gone, this is us working right through to March.

'When you look at those little blocks of games, and where the teams are, it's key that we just put our shoulder to the wheel.

'Every game is going to bring up different challenges and just because we're at Ibrox, it's an advantage, but it doesn't guarantee anything. We've got to use that advantage properly.

Industry observers note that 'As I say, we've got some fixtures now ahead of the cup final. Hopefully we can get into the cup final in good form and with some strong performances.'.

Venezuelan striker Kevin Kelsy could be in line to start against Aberdeen.

Kevin Kelsy could be in line for a bigger role this week after fatigue caused by his return from international duty limited his involvement in Saturday's win over Motherwell.

The Venezuela striker was only fit enough for a substitute appearance after enduring a gruelling journey back from a friendly in Russia, with Derek McInnes admitting the travel disruption had taken its toll.

'When you go away on international duty, they go to some far-flung places and playing a friendly in Russia is not the best preparation,' said the Rangers boss.

'There was a point on Thursday morning when we were really worried about whether he was getting back. To have ten-and-a-half hours in an airport all day Thursday isn't ideal preparation.

'He was gubbed on Friday. He was very tired when he spoke to me and told me he hadn't really slept.

'It's been a bit unusual, the preparation. We sent him home early on Friday to get a good sleep and look after himself, but we just made the call we thought was the right thing to do.

'We needed everybody at it on Saturday and we've got a big week ahead of us where he can play his part, hopefully from the start in one or two of these games.'.

The future of Virgil van Dijk continues to be a much-discussed talking point going into the winter months.

The legendary Liverpool captain will see his current contract expire next June as things stand, with the Dutchman on track to become a free agent just before his 36th birthday.

Transfer insider Graeme Bailey recently claimed that there’s a strong chance of the veteran defender being offered at least a 12-month extension at Anfield, with Andoni Iraola unsurprisingly keen to keep hold of his skipper.

In his latest Liverpool Confidential feature for the Daily Mail, Lewis Steele reported of fervent interest from Serie A in Van Dijk amid ongoing speculation over the centre-back’s future.

The journalist wrote: ‘One source told me this week that AC Milan and other Italian clubs have been sniffing around Van Dijk for some time, with talks ongoing internally at those sides.

‘Milan owner Gerry Cardinale and influential adviser Zlatan Ibrahimovic are mentioned to be huge admirers of Van Dijk, who turns 36 next summer.’.

While the Rossoneri appear determined to pounce on any uncertainty over Van Dijk’s future, Steele added that the 35-year-old is ‘keen’ to extend his contract at Liverpool.

(Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images).

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Any reports of interest in the Dutchman from other clubs will naturally trigger a level of concern among Reds supporters, but it’s natural that there’d be a queue of suitors for one of the best defenders of his (perhaps any) generation when he’s seven months away from becoming a free agent.

Until such time that a final decision is communicated by LFC, fans’ nerves will be frayed as to Van Dijk’s future. When we’ve already seen Mo Salah and Andy Robertson depart this year, the loss of another modern-day great in 2027 would represent a further gut punch for Kopites.

However, it’s worth remembering that when the Liverpool captain last penned a new contract in April 2025, he was just over two months away from leaving on a free, so he won’t panic even if there might be considerable gnashing of teeth outside of those involved in negotiations over his future.

James Pearce recently advised Reds supporters not to expect a ‘quick resolution’ over the defender’s situation, so for now, it seems that the best way for Van Dijk to secure a latest deal at Anfield is to maintain the strong performance levels he’s shown so far this season.

The noise over his future is sure to continue for the time being, but we remain confident that everything will come together in due course and that our iconic number 4 will continue to grace the famous red shirt in the 2027/28 campaign.

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc.

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Sources indicate that bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe.

To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and quickly.

How Noni Madueke grew into a unique piece at Arsenal amid injury absences

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1130 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Alexis Pereira | 23 Nov 2026 21:02.
  • Noni Madueke’s signing for Arsenal divided opinion before the forward had played a game.
  • A little more than a year later, the discussion is taking on another dimension.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Alexis Pereira | 23 Nov 2026 21:02.

Noni Madueke’s signing for Arsenal divided opinion before the forward had played a game. Signed from Chelsea for £50m, the Englishman joined a squad that already had Bukayo Saka as the owner of the right wing, and he had to justify an investment in a player who initially appeared destined to be a back-up.

A little more than a year later, the discussion is taking on another dimension. With Saka injured, Madueke received a longer run of opportunities and took the space. As well as goals and assists, he has contributed in different roles on both sides of the pitch. The 2-2 draw with Newcastle United, in which he scored the goal that earned Arsenal a point, was another example of that growth.

Mikel Arteta has noticed a change that goes beyond productivity. In his press conference, the boss highlighted the variety the forward has added to the game and his involvement without the ball.

Industry observers note that madueke has very specific characteristics. Left-footed and explosive, he likes to receive wide on the right, run at the full-back and carry the ball towards the box to shoot or find a team-mate. His short acceleration and ability to change direction make his movements hard to defend when he receives in one-on-one situations.

Recent findings suggest that that characteristic was already visible at Chelsea. In 2024-25, he was one of the Premier League players who progressed the ball towards the box the most and created danger mainly through individual carries. The problem was inconsistency in execution: he did not always choose the best moment. Arteta acknowledged the change.

‘He is becoming decisive in games, and that is what we need from our forwards,’ Arteta said. ‘And he is doing it in various ways, which is something I really like. He has added variety and much more connection to his game.’.

It has been revealed that the numbers help show the scale of the growth. According to FotMob’s Premier League 2026-27 data, Madueke creates 3.6 chances per 90 minutes, against 1.5 for Saka. It is a significant difference, although Saka has played fewer minutes. The growth also indicates in his ability to contribute without the ball. According to Arteta, Madueke does not always need to receive the ball at his feet to take part in the move.

‘And yes, I also love his intensity without the ball,’ Arteta noted. ‘So I would say he is becoming a much more complete player, and I think he is enjoying that a lot.’.

The development is therefore not about abandoning the dribble, but knowing when to use it. Madueke remains a player of individual initiative, but now seems to understand better how his actions can connect with the collective workings of the team.

Comparison with Saka is inevitable, but the two are not identical. Both are left-footed and prefer to start from the right and move inside, but they do it in different ways. Saka is more refined in decision-making. He has excellent ball control, protects possession under pressure and moves naturally between carries, short passes and crosses. His ability to draw two markers and find the free team-mate is also one of Arsenal’s main attacking tools.

Madueke offers more explosion in the first movement and tends to seek one-on-one duels more often. He is more vertical, liking to accelerate and attack the space left by the full-back. When confident, he can disorganise a defence without relying on a long build-up.

Industry observers note that the creation data help illustrate the difference. As well as beating Saka for chances created per 90 minutes in FotMob’s numbers, Madueke also demonstrates a higher volume of dribbles and progressive carries per minute in another statistical comparison this season. Saka, on the other hand, keeps an advantage in shooting and defensive involvement. They are complementary profiles, not necessarily competitors for a single way of playing.

Recent findings suggest that that difference is valuable for Arteta. Against opponents who defend in a low block, Saka may be more useful to control possession, combine with the midfielders and find the pass that breaks down the marking. Madueke can offer a more direct threat, attacking the full-back and creating individual imbalances.

The Englishman has also shown he can play on the left, a role he took on when Christos Tzolis was absent. There he must adapt his movements: instead of cutting inside with his dominant foot, he can go to the byline and cross with his right. It is not necessarily his ideal position, but the versatility widens Arteta’s options and stops the team depending on a single alternative for each side.

The competition with Saka does not need to be seen as an attempt to remove the starter. Arsenal need more than one player able to decide matches, especially in a long season with the Premier League, Champions League and domestic cups. The point is that Madueke is beginning to offer arguments to be considered more than simple cover.

In a recent development, one detail of this transformation happened away from Arsenal. After being left out of an England squad, Madueke decided to use the international break to train individually. Instead of treating the period as a chance to rest, the forward sought out a specific preparation programme.

Arteta highlighted the player’s reaction as an example to the rest of the squad. The boss said Madueke came back from the break as a different athlete, determined not to accept the situation he was in.

‘He went to train and came back a different Noni,’ Arteta explained. ‘He was not willing to accept that situation and showed he was determined. Since then, it has been incredible.’.

The individual work did not start now, however. In an interview with Sky Sports, Madueke revealed that he has worked for years with specialist coach Saul Isaksson-Hurst, since his time at PSV. The partnership involves technical improvement and individual development, with special attention on being more decisive in the final third.

The result has shown in the numbers: his average of chances created more than doubled compared with the previous season, reaching 3.57 per 90 minutes in the Premier League. His dribble success rate rose from 50 per cent to 55 per cent, while his pass accuracy went from 78 per cent to 87 per cent. In open-play crosses, his success rate jumped from 14 per cent to 33 per cent.

Those numbers help explain why Arteta speaks of a more complete player. Madueke has not stopped looking for the dribble, but has begun to execute other actions better, which could previously limit his influence. The growth combined different reasons and paths, but the result has arrived and is evident in the current season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s now coming up to six months since Arne Slot was relieved of his duties as Liverpool head coach after two years in the role.

The Dutchman had the unenviable task of succeeding Jurgen Klopp in the Anfield dugout but delivered a surprise (and emphatic) Premier League title triumph in his first season in charge before the Reds’ fortunes nosedived dramatically last term.

The 48-year-old just about managed to achieve Champions League qualification in May, but the extent of the decline from 12 months previously made his position untenable, and he was dismissed to make way for Andoni Iraola.

In his latest Liverpool Confidential feature for the Daily Mail, Lewis Steele addressed the question of what Slot has been getting up to since his exit from Anfield, with the journalist ‘often asked’ about the Dutch tactician’s more recent endeavours.

He outlined that the former Reds boss has been ‘biding his time and enjoying holidays with loved ones’, including multiple trips to Ibiza and taking in football matches in Argentina and Brazil with his son Joep, along with attending games in his native Netherlands.

Sources indicate that the 48-year-old turned down the chance to coach his country after the World Cup, as well as potentially ‘lucrative gig’ in Saudi Arabia. He also declined approaches from a few clubs in the summer, including AC Milan, who now have ex-Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim in charge.

Steele concluded that Slot is ‘waiting for the right opportunity’ to get back into the dugout and doesn’t believe that his ‘stock has fallen’ as much as some of his peers who’ve been sacked by other high-profile Premier League clubs.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

The Dutchman’s Liverpool tenure may have ended on a low ebb, and the prevailing sentiment in May was that the time was right for a change, but it’d be wrong to describe his two-year spell at Anfield as a failure.

He vastly exceeded expectations by winning the Premier League at the first attempt, and while last season was undoubtedly a massive underachievement results-wise, it must be viewed in the context of Slot and the squad trying to navigate the horrendous grief of Diogo Jota’s tragic death.

That the 48-year-old has turned down job approaches in order to hold out for the ‘right opportunity’ indicates his confidence that he’ll get back on board the managerial carousel sooner rather than later, and that his reputation hasn’t been overly tarnished by the disappointment of 2025/26.

Most Liverpool fans would also acknowledge that Slot carried himself with tremendous dignity throughout his time with us, striking the perfect tone with his farewell message to supporters after his sacking and – most importantly – handling the loss of Jota with commendable grace.

It’s nice to hear that the Dutchman has been enjoying his time with family since departing Merseyside, and it wouldn’t surprise us in the slightest if he were to be back in the technical area with a newly introduced club over the next few months.

Wherever his career might take him from here, we wish him the best in his future endeavours.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: William D. Nordhaus obituary: economist whose tools transformed climate policy

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (769 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Credit: Monica Jorge/Latest York Times/Redux/eyevine.
  • William (Bill) Nordhaus was an economist known for introducing climate change into economic analysis, earning him the 2018 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences.
  • His research shaped our understanding of what drives economic growth and innovation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Credit: Monica Jorge/Latest York Times/Redux/eyevine.

William (Bill) Nordhaus was an economist known for introducing climate change into economic analysis, earning him the 2018 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences. Profoundly curious and able to distill complex concerns to their core, Nordhaus produced groundbreaking scholarship powered by his joy of discovery, dedication to getting things right and commitment to ensuring that science serves society.

His research shaped our understanding of what drives economic growth and innovation. He realized that omitting the environment from economic measurement would send the wrong signals about the directions of economic growth and, therefore, pioneered more-inclusive ways to measure growth.

To build a better world, stop chasing economic growth.

To build a better world, stop chasing economic growth.

Nordhaus was born in Albuquerque, Newly introduced Mexico. His father developed a ski area to the east of the city, and as a child, Nordhaus tried to derive models of snowfall. He earned an undergraduate degree in economics from Yale University in New Haven, Connecticut, in 1963, before moving to the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in Cambridge, where he completed his PhD in 1967 under the supervision of future Nobel prizewinner Robert Solow. He then returned to Yale as an assistant professor and spent the rest of his academic career there.

According to recent reports, nordhaus swiftly made a name for himself by developing an early rigorous model for endogenous growth — that which occurs inside an economic system, rather than being driven by external factors. Before then, economic models had assumed that the rate of change in technology was independent of the economy.

In a recent development, nordhaus’s PhD work showed that the pace of innovation depended on economic incentives, which could be altered by policy, such as through the patent system. His model also projected that research would face diminishing returns, with newly introduced ideas getting harder to find — an idea that was validated 40 years later.

Why we need an International Panel on Inequality.

Why we need an International Panel on Inequality.

Next, he questioned the nature of economic growth. He recalled being inspired by an article in an in-flight magazine that described gross national product (GNP) as gross national pollution. In a 1972 article titled ‘Is Growth Obsolete?’, Nordhaus and economist James Tobin wrote that GNP exaggerates economic benefits by omitting environmental damage by “treating as free things which are not really free” and that “this practice gives the wrong signals for the directions of economic growth”. GNP also understates some of the benefits of economic growth, such as increased household well-being, from inventions such as electricity and home appliances.

This work alone gave rise to three influential lines of research: climate economics, the role of national accounts in measuring sustainable development and the importance of including fresh goods in measures of national income and economic well-being.

In a recent development, nordhaus also considered the role of innovation. In a 1996 article on the history of the price of lighting, he measured the output and cost of various sources of light across human history (see go.nature.com/478rjyh). He revealed that the light output per unit of energy of the compact fluorescent bulb was about 30,000 times greater than that of our distant ancestors’ fire.

How countries can grow without impoverishing future generations.

How countries can grow without impoverishing future generations.

With Wirtz operating in the number 10 role, Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola are the names in the frame out wide, with the latter hoping to find the back of the net after missing a number of chances against the Red Devils.

Cody Gakpo is a doubt after picking up a calf injury on international duty with the Netherlands, while 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha could begin the game on the bench for load management reasons, following his record-breaking goal and assist against Man United.

  • How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.
